### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Question · hash: sha256:a00ab55a893ba5826da676e75ca9ac21e9687d05c8105625d3228aa82906410b*

`nomos work abandon` has always refused without `--reason`. `ReleaseOutcome::Abandoned`
has always carried `reason: String` non-optionally — the same technique the doc comment
directly above it praises the finished arm for, where carrying the `VerificationRecord` in
the variant is what makes a finished item structurally impossible without evidence.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Question · hash: sha256:5bbf0884f4d66bb8f5d8d96109a3a17c3212673e34767dea1f6b6f3345e797af*

Then `FileLedger::Release` matched it with `{ .. }` and set the state and nothing else, in
the arm adjacent to the one writing `verified = Some(record)`. One match, two arms, one
keeping its evidence and one discarding it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Question · hash: sha256:a01f0cc81d73db50506535e61cb64fde84024cb46407b0556ee60607d1868752*

So the question is not whether an abandonment should be recorded. Every layer above the
store already behaved as though it were. The question is why one of the two reasons this
ledger asks for survives and the other does not.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What The Difference Actually Is · hash: sha256:d187a1015ac28c0d00e2af127522d6a7463d90be6ae8d44ac3d45d473591f80b*

## What The Difference Actually Is

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What The Difference Actually Is · hash: sha256:cad965cf77554b5017713c103e89dbd7fc4f975477aea1c49bb5017dcc7a60aa*

`ItemState::Declined` carries a reason, and its doc comment says why: so an item cannot be
declined reasonlessly. That reason survives every write, and nobody had to arrange it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What The Difference Actually Is · hash: sha256:8d4f1be53e057a32b952302d3f3bc4785ecc5652383f667cea7f80b66390a47a*

It survives because it is part of a **state**. States are what a ledger persists. A
transition is not persisted at all — it happens, it produces a new state, and whatever it
was carrying is gone unless something on the item was given the job of holding it. Nothing
had been.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What The Difference Actually Is · hash: sha256:8131feeafa96eb0ac91a9e3ab6f0631dad5a797819005448bc82a9edda847c4f*

That is the whole of the defect, and it generalizes past this field: any evidence a
transition carries needs somewhere on the record to land, or the type system's insistence
on carrying it buys nothing beyond the function call. The signature made the reason
impossible to omit and could not make it impossible to drop.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent · hash: sha256:2d3df9e1acf60853cd7b56aa260e51c47a361b9deaa536e3c3a90daef4970b9b*

## Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent · hash: sha256:5cc200d515b15ef1239f27d01fde19518bf7cbe62b7cd8ce8feee3d03ef236c6*

`item.rs` says a lapsed claim does not release itself, and stays visible "so that a person
can see the work was abandoned rather than never started". The crate root says the same.
That is a deliberate decision to keep evidence of work that stopped.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent · hash: sha256:a9e1bf4b43192445162e8277659b03eddb7b4a26c242e496cfabc16ec8f47940*

Against it: an agent that died holding a claim left that claim behind, visible. An agent
that stopped deliberately — having been compelled to write down why — left nothing at all.
The claim went to `None`, the item went back to `Ready`, and afterwards the item did not
say it had ever been held.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent · hash: sha256:aa4d4ee6f033e1395446882a42f52941d7c731bc4c341529ba4cc461c8242db2*

The well-behaved path was the lossy one. That is worse than an oversight, because it
selects against the behaviour the ledger asks for: the more correctly an agent shut down,
the less of it survived.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Why It Inverted The Crate's Own Intent · hash: sha256:b1860187b5543233a575eb1fc92967633e9f29c4b1b2bd491aec56eecfb734ae*

Observed on 2026-08-09 releasing `P9-ONE-DIRECTION`. The reason given said where the work
had reached and why it stopped, and it survives only in the message of commit `a749f9a` —
the half-recorded shape `OD-SPEC-005` exists to name.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:e9694a3194f2f446d55bcb0911ee7ad0ca15a959b3400a958940efe0735a6806*

An abandonment is recorded on the item it happened to: who stopped, why, and when.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:d612e5377dbd6fbdcbdba8d4fb403d95a798deeb1fb46ef75112aac063401692*

**It is a list, not a field.** An item abandoned twice was abandoned twice. Keeping only
the most recent would discard the earlier reason, which is this same defect one scale down.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:c77cafc289a45b7a885993584bfb57080f03cec256b08e328e2fc64f245d22d9*

**Both arms of a release are written once**, in `ReleaseOutcome::Record_On`, next to the
type that carries the evidence — the reason `Refusal_From` exists in the same crate. This
is not defensive: the defect *was* an implementation spelling the rule out for itself and
spelling one arm of it correctly. A second `ExclusionLedger` — the run-scoped and
session-scoped instances this crate's scope section anticipates — would have been free to
reproduce it exactly.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:d7b6e2887298ab78524af3df9d2906c51860596d8e44652dfdaa671947544962*

**It is reported, not merely stored.** `nomos work show` reports one item, because `list`
is a column per item and cannot carry prose. A record no surface reports is a record only
somebody willing to read the JSON will find, which is most of the way back to not keeping
it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Decision · hash: sha256:cd4fdd015a69a4325d7fa12d9ed975d0d63380420be5441011537db4de22922e*

**Ending the claim is part of recording the abandonment**, rather than left to the caller.
An abandonment is a record of something that stopped; a record that went on excluding
people would be a worse defect than the one it replaced.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Lapsed Claim, Settled · hash: sha256:66c98506341e9997c4cc27685883ec655dc69d0d5711cb2daf05aa31f0ea91b8*

## The Lapsed Claim, Settled

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Lapsed Claim, Settled · hash: sha256:9fd5504f82b589862dddb04d9ad9a17fbc0ed25a0b75014f82d0c4ec6794cb17*

A lapsed claim is given **no** synthesized abandonment.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Lapsed Claim, Settled · hash: sha256:466e79c671f01a1a4cef5d02e008f984bbd967298982196b9ddf16826c7f8a6c*

Nobody was there to write a reason. Writing "the lease expired" would be inventing the one
field that exists to hold what a person actually said — filler wearing a record's clothes,
which this repository already refuses elsewhere for placeholder records.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Lapsed Claim, Settled · hash: sha256:b7062bfe0ac28d1f9ccd869b8eb0f8a3f0f95827b578035c7d274c5f1606f0f4*

What a lapse leaves is the claim itself, still on the item, which says who held it and
when they stopped. So both paths now leave a record, and they differ by what is genuinely
knowable rather than by which code path ran. That is the asymmetry that should exist.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / The Lapsed Claim, Settled · hash: sha256:b8f6f5388110e107cbd0bab940d9ee4cbcf0d7065de324aff41b6d051188e54c*

*(Amended at version 2. This paragraph said the claim is "still on the item", which stopped
being the whole truth once an item could be taken over: something has to replace it.
`OD-LEDGER-012` moves it to `LedgerItem::displaced` rather than dropping it, and moves the
claim itself rather than a summary of it — so what this paragraph protects is unchanged and
only where it points has moved. No `reason` field is created for a lapse there either, for the
reason given above: nobody was present to write one. See the amendment note below.)*

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:145a4bc3c8b210a7aeda91b2af32403f57bef7f678d01af690e89b0ea05cfa8a*

## What This Found And Did Not Fix

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:bc734c0fc07adfa9efc48181cbdbbe7b587455115dba88b91e7a0530cace136f*

A lapse does not make the item takeable again.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:27a085a3b4a8882af0d2f6a27896cb6a15ad39e640731d96c3ce6657d49ff4a9*

*(Amended at version 2. That sentence is superseded: a lapse still does not make an item
**claimable**, and `claim` still refuses it, but `OD-LEDGER-012` makes it **takeable** by a verb
of its own, `nomos work takeover`. The rest of this section is the measurement that opened
`P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER` and is kept as it was written. See the amendment note below.)*

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:61437ab9bb5c7d44c454123b217492f7cd35aac0cd963074db624b38b1753e5d*

`item.rs` says a lapsed claim "stops excluding, which is what lets the next agent take the
item". The first half is true: `Has_Active_Claim` goes false, so the lapsed claim stops
being counted against *other* items' territory. The second half is not. A lapse leaves
`state` at `Claimed`, and `Claim_Refusal` rejects anything that is not `Ready` before it
ever looks at a lease — so the lapsed item itself can never be re-claimed until somebody
edits the file by hand. `MAXIMUM_LEASE` exists so that "an agent which died at lunchtime
does not hold territory until tomorrow", and for its own item that is not what happens.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:b4aa35f7ff0dcc1f8dc1f03531bf21131be0ebb49f4dc970c6e1a2d6d6134b4e*

Nothing asserted it. The two lapse tests check `Has_Active_Claim` and check that `Validate`
reports no overlap; neither takes the item.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:ecb71e9462cb65ed295775a77406e33945e42e95896cbca40a7c9e3924d0895e*

It is left unfixed here deliberately. It is a different defect with a different decision
behind it — whether a lapse should return an item to `Ready`, and what that costs an agent
that is merely slow rather than dead — and it is on the ledger rather than in this
sentence. The test written here asserts the reason and the visibility and stops short of
the claimability, because an assertion either way would pin the behaviour in place before
that decision is made.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#32

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / What This Found And Did Not Fix · hash: sha256:1bc74ad586a3067d625036f51e339f80a871d681598a47d09fcf5028c45b215b*

*(Amended at version 2. That decision is now made, in `OD-LEDGER-012`, and it is neither of the
two shapes this paragraph anticipated: a lapse does not return the item to `Ready`, and what it
costs an agent that is merely slow is bounded by that agent's own lease rather than by a policy.
The test did exactly what this paragraph says it was for — it is renamed and its refusal
assertion re-pointed, and the assertion that the lapsed claim was not replaced is kept word for
word. See the amendment note below.)*

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#33

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#34

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Consequences · hash: sha256:259eb6194d6c927b9bc9840b90403b4ad8913a8c4bb689954cd0ee1c0868dd50*

Every item written before this field existed has no abandonments, and `#[serde(default)]`
leaves it that way. That is a fact about those items rather than something to backfill.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#35

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Consequences · hash: sha256:dd0df4a165a813cf6fae5257ebb589dd8b7165ca547daab135e9456b41cbf3f8*

The reason is prose, and prose is not queryable. `Blocker` is a typed enum precisely
because storing "why" as a sentence made it impossible to ask how much of the backlog was
waiting on a person. The same objection applies here and is accepted rather than answered:
an abandonment is a narrative addressed to the next agent, and the shapes worth counting
are not yet known. If they turn out to be countable, they can be typed later against real
examples instead of guessed at now.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#36

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:5cb944a4a1301e8ad3517f1765a04a3f16c2d31cb5ec1b14acf903dbfedfe51e*

## Amendment, Version 2

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#37

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:ad3691edbdff38e445701c77a8e851bbb3c8385f7a0edda983be2531b44b7fbf*

`P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER` reopened this record deliberately, which its own `done_when` required of
it: *"`OD-LEDGER-006` is reopened deliberately or it is not touched."* `OD-LEDGER-012` carries
the new decision and this note records what moved here.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#38

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:3c9b95b66aaf55061b2652e7e21dab5484863f15570c5fada5610b220681c24e*

**What changed is where a lapse's evidence lives once something displaces it.** This record
decided that the evidence of stopped work must survive, and it left a lapse's evidence in the
one place that needed no arranging: the claim, still on the item. A takeover needs that slot, so
the claim moves to `LedgerItem::displaced` — a list, oldest first, holding each displaced claim
exactly as it stood. `LedgerItem::Replace_Lapsed_Claim` performs the move and the install as one
operation, which is this record's own `ReleaseOutcome::Record_On` technique applied to the field
it created: an implementation free to spell one half of a rule at its call site eventually
spells one half.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#39

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:40d3daed1d3c7129da781b1160e7ac90fafdf73aba7121ddd704fefc3d02f4cd*

**What did not change is the rule that put it there.** A lapse still gets no synthesized
reason, because there is still nobody who gave one. `Abandonment::reason` remains the words the
holder gave, `displaced` has no `reason` field to fill, and the criterion this record
established — a transition's evidence survives only where something on the item is given the job
of holding it, and only what somebody actually knew at the time is held — is what chose the
shape of the new field rather than being weakened by it. `OD-LEDGER-012` states that criterion
in this record's terms and applies it to a transition nobody was present for.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#40

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:5ee5596838ab20d0ed94c4e238933e94985687bdb820d0e2b995ecd2b3cc1d71*

**What was found here and deferred is closed.** The section above measured that a lapsed item
was unreachable by anybody and said so rather than fixing it, on the ground that the fix was a
different decision. That was correct and the deferral held for exactly as long as it should
have: the decision is made in a record of its own, and the behaviour this record's test declined
to pin is now pinned by that record's tests.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#41

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:81ee84432edbff2c912d6785dcfe1753c217e8fe2e57492e31ef473a025cc9d0*

The decision this record is *about* is untouched. A reason attached to a state survives and one
attached to a transition does not, and that is why this record is amended in place rather than
superseded — a `superseded_by` edge would tell a later reader the whole of it is dead.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-006-a-reason-attached-to-a-transition-does-not-survive-it.md#42

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Status · hash: sha256:8b1501efecf5aaab88f0940d5804c94111b5c227a27bc5fd9a3e96cca6744236*

## Status

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Status · hash: sha256:f4f426eec0be9c587ed8f45a82fa5a3636eb7b2b30bffe5e456600b00a341032*

Accepted. Implemented in `nomos-ledger` and reported by `nomos work show`.

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A reason attached to a transition does not survive it, and a reason attached to a state does / Status · hash: sha256:c72f4ec5d4ec372e9cd440c611e84b06e9490f67ecfc3cc9e34ae1b94407066a*

# A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Question · hash: sha256:d2210bb38b5618c989422d8241ac9ef50428e3ee881d827271604e13307b8ad8*

`P10-RECORD-LOCK` set out to stop a record reservation from serializing the board. Before
it, every open item reserved `docs/records`, which contains every record anybody could
write, so one claim refused all eight others. It re-authored each item to reserve the
record identifier it would allocate, and it left behind an acceptance test:
`Test_Two_Items_Writing_Different_Records_Should_Be_Claimable_At_Once`, asserted against the
repository's own `work/ledger.json`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Question · hash: sha256:259f9bc0e4d59f9cfa8bd5b6e41578e7e7201adcccd43e60a1c9af066502798c*

That test went red on 2026-08-09 with no code change. Five open items reserved a record and
no two of them could be held at once, so the search for a pair found none and both
assertions failed on their own precondition rather than on their subject.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Question · hash: sha256:b65ae90c138c1059352caa875734be874261ddd5ceb2d3b25f686f21ef1eaaf3*

The reason is not who authored what. It is a rule.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Two Rules, Each Forcing A Shared Edit · hash: sha256:893538151eeb12eef60bcd8232f240ddeac9bee31921993aade1b46030691d88*

## Two Rules, Each Forcing A Shared Edit

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Two Rules, Each Forcing A Shared Edit · hash: sha256:8cd8a6ec23e641c66f352eff96f963ad5b8356e93c8d8ffebfef40ec5374ac95*

**Seeding.** `OD-LEDGER-001`'s third authoring rule requires that anything writing a
canonical record also reserve `crates/spec/nomos-spec-store`, because a canonical record
must be added to `RECORDS` and `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS` in `governing.rs` and the literal
count in `governing_records_are_present.rs` raised, or the workspace goes red. Two items
writing two *different* records therefore edit the same two files. They cannot be
independent, by construction — and the rule that makes it so was added in the same body of
work as the guarantee it defeats.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Two Rules, Each Forcing A Shared Edit · hash: sha256:5851685899d96167a2aa196aa7b0d5de708d7807f3b16a02f290042c40170ed6*

**Snapshots.** `P9-PUBLIC-API` checks each crate's public surface into
`tests/contract/surface`, and `corpus_gates.rs` declares a per-file test count. So an item
that widens any API, or adds any test to a corpus-gated file, writes under `tests/contract`
— and items reserve the whole directory in order to write one file inside it. That is
exactly the shape `P10-RECORD-LOCK` named for records, one level up, arriving independently
and later.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Two Rules, Each Forcing A Shared Edit · hash: sha256:17899c81dc616e07a307cc5d244a1e160da4b32ffe44e62d13f4f294cf24c290*

`OD-LEDGER-004` measured both without drawing the conclusion. It lists `crates/spec` and
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store` at six blocked pairs and `tests/contract` at five, and reads
them as ordinary code contention. For record-writing items specifically they are not: the
overlap is guaranteed by an authoring rule, so the acceptance test passed only for as long
as some pair on the board happened to be disjoint for unrelated reasons. The property was
measured true once and was never structurally maintained.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:9aedad06dfde7be7388995935696ea6e7090d9f569ce7b8ea692e7506295325f*

**The acceptance property is restated to the one the mechanism can keep: a record excludes
nobody but its own writer. What else two record writers share is measured separately, and
every path *all* of them are forced to reserve must be declared.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:2cc77dc952129b439f5e644afa88f5dd328637de6553c17cbf7bac3c14d08e88*

Three tests carry it, in `crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/records_do_not_serialize.rs`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:89d2cdf7bed8914487e5b01853a90983814ea6658552e9afb88bf48bb20decbf*

**`Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer`** reduces every open record
writer to the records it reserves and claims all of them through the real ledger on that
projection. All, not a pair: a pair could be independent by accident. This is exactly what
`P10-RECORD-LOCK` bought and it holds for a structural reason — an item reserves
`docs/records/<ID>` and two identifiers are two paths.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:4fc77cd628f5105fabec288a38f5c7e0356b42a6de7f101c6a661090df170c82*

**`Test_Every_Universal_Reservation_Should_Be_Declared`** is the new guard. A path two
record writers share is *contention*: two items that both change the CLI, which is what
territory is for and which resolves when one of them finishes. A path **all** of them
reserve is a *rule*, and it does not resolve — the next record writer will reserve it too.
Those are enumerated in `KNOWN_SERIALIZERS` with what forces each, and a third one arriving
fails the suite.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:bd1ea7960036b57f5220110e3209d6688d748698edcab169241c372fd0c7c3cf*

**`Test_Every_Declared_Serializer_Should_Still_Serialize`** is the other direction. A
register that over-reports is as useless as one that under-reports, so an entry that stops
serializing anything has to come out in the commit that earned it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / The Decision · hash: sha256:13dff712a4b46b67e7c132d1a51176898727f9d0cf0f1439f7ff27e2dd7e8b19*

The register is a debt list, not an exemption list. It is expected to empty.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here · hash: sha256:8a7b585cb4d6b33a9379f0917bba050c15c3fd76557f0b5d3333cd341ef7fca8*

## Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here · hash: sha256:0bbfd3859c1db144b5ceac56a4d37f16efce60c791e0aa606b865a37dbb1e89a*

The structural fix for seeding is to derive `RECORDS` and `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS` from
`docs/records` rather than hand-maintaining them. That would remove the shared edit
entirely: adding a record would touch the record file and nothing else.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here · hash: sha256:e98773502a832649709e38deeae5e3a1d450e5fd950ec7fb56475f4e5f7ca8b8*

It is not done here, for a reason rather than for time. The hand-maintained list *is* a
declared universe, and the literal count assertion is the deliberate cost of adding a
governing record. `OD-SPEC-005` exists because six governing records were written as files
and never reached the store — the declaration is what catches that, and deriving the list
would make `Test_Every_Canonical_Record_On_Disk_Should_Be_Governing` compare a directory
against itself and pass having checked nothing. Replacing a universe with a derivation is
`OD-COMPLETENESS-001`'s subject and overlaps `P10-MIRROR-DISAGREEMENT`, which is open and
holds the same question about `DECLARED_RULES`. Two items deriving two universes by two
methods is how they come to disagree, so it wants coordinating rather than doing twice.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here · hash: sha256:8f73ef78297eb35361c41f0e159f5a9026b4cd642fd623faa0222e2e8a311c46*

The structural fix for snapshots is finer reservation: an item that changes one crate's API
reserves `tests/contract/surface/<crate>.txt`, not the directory. Nothing prevents that
today — territory is file-resolution and already compares paths by containment. What is
*not* done here is forcing it, because forcing it means re-authoring four items that
belong to other work, and `P10-SEEDING-SERIALIZES` explicitly refuses to manufacture a pair
by narrowing somebody else's territory.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / What This Costs · hash: sha256:50e8d3d1d6c4a24186d6e6a0bd26f4a9d0b928104cf0c665f864e60eda7c8cd4*

## What This Costs

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / What This Costs · hash: sha256:11e515127f466dca755d84910cb7421ab058a6a40548b10b9e68549105169454*

The board serializes and will keep serializing. At the time of this record: five open
record writers, ten pairs, ten blocked — seven of them by nothing but the two declared
serializers, and three by ordinary code contention as well. Those seven are the debt.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / What This Costs · hash: sha256:e2a1326114e5221a4cc2f66999ea96da54a4c806ad92185c32e6926913f015f3*

What is bought is that the number is measured on every run and printed beside its
denominator, the two causes are told apart, and a third cause cannot arrive quietly. What
is given up is the claim that the board is parallel today, which was never true for a
reason anybody had arranged.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Status · hash: sha256:8b1501efecf5aaab88f0940d5804c94111b5c227a27bc5fd9a3e96cca6744236*

## Status

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record excludes nobody, and the two files that still serialize the board are declared / Status · hash: sha256:ee577626ddfdd8ed2748766c88a5efe3f566b1c25c83f9c808e79d1a92b79d7e*

Closed by `P10-SEEDING-SERIALIZES`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#1

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back · hash: sha256:a150d4a15a3b8ba0b80b0ee5fd17f091a64a472105b3ce33db516420fb386f9b*

# A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Question · hash: sha256:03647b40598fa30a17123f02f95b27768a52c5ccb01107e3dd790499ca9bba04*

`LedgerItem` and `LedgerDocument` derived `Deserialize` with serde's default behaviour, which is
to ignore any key the type does not declare. `SCHEMA_VERSION` existed and was read at exactly one
site — filling in the document returned for a file that is not there. `Load` never compared it.
`Save` re-serialized whatever `Load` produced.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Question · hash: sha256:1c7e667217a0d4778da14dd0e712da66383095042f9a402fee5bb63fb3542062*

Compose those three and a `nomos.exe` built before a field existed reads the current
`work/ledger.json`, drops every key added since, writes the result back, and exits 0. The state
change survives. The data does not. A lossy write and a clean one are the same event at the
surface that reports them.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Evidence · hash: sha256:4304963d62d201a473a5dcdfdc689cf14aa577c87c2932120e97ceaa34a5f125*

## The Evidence

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Evidence · hash: sha256:9e628bcc92dcfb6d94d0c228d796ac2b23a579d63da8aeb1b6a87ce858b5a2a6*

Not inferred. An abandonment reason for `P10-ABANDON-REASON` was written at unix 1786326402
through a freshly built binary and was gone by 1786326839, when another session's `work claim`
rewrote the file. The release stood; the reason did not.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Evidence · hash: sha256:550a8d5c097dbbfd3a7d459b6c23f7efe42809ec7270e574e1fd38c44e545932*

It had been happening since the field was introduced. Commit `e88f92d` added
`LedgerItem::abandoned` with `serde(default)` and no `skip_serializing_if`, so a current binary
emits the key on every item — and both `e88f92d` and `6326566` committed a `work/ledger.json`
containing zero of them. The session that added the field was stripping it as it wrote it, in the
commit that added it, and nothing said so.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Evidence · hash: sha256:c5990b2c645332972443014b0ba4d69d9d2bd364a522a21948209760a46d84d5*

What produced it is a documented workaround rather than carelessness. `work finish` cannot run
under `cargo run`, because the predicate rebuilds the executable that is the running process, so
sessions copy `target/debug/nomos.exe` and run the copy. A copy taken before a schema change is a
stale writer for the rest of that session. A workaround for a file lock became a silent
data-loss channel on a file two sessions share.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Evidence · hash: sha256:0d514e3d95a894e5ceec36208103b41c9ee1e0a4405fddb822cd57398ec3c9cf*

`Test_The_Ledger_Should_Round_Trip_Losslessly` could not see any of it. It builds a `LedgerItem`
in Rust, saves it, loads it and compares, so every key in that file is a key the type declares.
It asserted that the *declared* shape survives, which was never in question.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Shape · hash: sha256:ee2a26402381c7a765a8f7e0550d385a07dfefc3e3c7e2835d4b34ac4e5dd810*

## The Shape

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Shape · hash: sha256:a74e50e2dc92dcfcb854f273674040569e6187644cd943f9af84cd885968844c*

`OD-LEDGER-006` one level down. That record is about a reason attached to a transition not
surviving it. This is a reason attached to an *item* not surviving the next *writer*, and it fails
the same way, by looking like success.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Shape · hash: sha256:29e8a99d322c5d902fcedc68a64dfc79bf6ef817f2842e25226fac8b9e542a40*

`OD-LEDGER-009` named the third instance of a reason destroyed by the failure it explains. This is
the fourth, and the most complete, because here the failure has no report at all.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:8abc66481dea8e91ecff7153fc19dadddeb3bb7a99aba2531f4cae859d8f25d8*

## Three Remedies Were Available

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:d07f7a892236a5b0bd787bde07494aa97022e27cdf67fe4c58d780bbf35e10d2*

**A schema version compared on load.** Cheap — two lines and an error arm — and it produces the
best sentence an operator could read. Refused as the *guarantee* for one reason: nothing forces
the bump. `e88f92d` added a field and raised nothing, so a guard whose completeness rests on the
discipline that already failed will report clean on the next instance of the defect it was built
for. Absence of a bump would become success. It is also coarse: it answers "is this file newer
than me" and never "is there a key here I am about to destroy".

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:ebcb5c7ebe1903e601e43a78d5ab8dc2a8116c1c2e7c6b8ac3616da18db7e3a2*

**A capture map, preserving unknown keys through a `serde(flatten)` map.** It makes an old binary
*correct* rather than merely loud, which is a stronger guarantee than the one adopted here, and it
is refused anyway.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:534225ca59dfdf264d44717476fac3c96fbd3c41c6e0b2b29242891025b255ca*

Three costs, the last decisive. It is silent: a stale writer keeps working and nothing anywhere
reports that one is present, when an undetected stale writer is what caused the incident. It
cannot coexist with `deny_unknown_fields` on the same type, so adopting it trades away detection
of a *misspelled* key permanently — measured in a standalone probe: under a capture map,
`{"clam": {…}}` parses with `claim: None` and the misspelling parked in the map, where before it
was at least discarded and under the adopted remedy it is refused outright.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:3b52ccdb1685cb75b6f747a7f7438b4063101efd0bdcf1c24de1b6ebe5e62c75*

And it promises more than it can keep. Preserving a key preserves bytes, not meaning. Nothing in
this crate can know whether the key it copied through changes the meaning of the keys it does
understand — a later `frozen` or `superseded_by` would be carried forward faithfully by a binary
that then acts as though it were not there. "An old binary round-trips correctly" is a guarantee
larger than what preservation demonstrates.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Three Remedies Were Available · hash: sha256:c6cb4c333b915d71679fdafed344f5b991cd9a41c1629c88880a7bcad371b9bc*

**Refusing to read a document that carries anything unaccounted for.** Adopted, because it is the
only one of the three that both prevents the loss **and** makes the stale writer visible at the
moment it tries.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:e2817dfc92ae254cb43fd749560c9de22f01d86d7a52249fd12374524a9db954*

**A build that cannot account for every key in the ledger does not write the ledger.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:78a4ced5554947e549eb969a46fa1530f5c73a1f9aa1709595fab2a67c8da4f8*

`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` on every deserialized container reachable from `LedgerDocument`:
the document, `LedgerItem`, `Territory`, `Claim`, `Abandonment`, `VerificationPredicate`,
`VerificationRecord`, `GateOutcome`, and the two enums `ItemState` and `Blocker`, whose struct
variants it also covers.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:6f59197044325c6595aaf4bdbd4a8460daaca52b0b23cc289d0d084991a11c31*

This is the crate's own rule applied to its own deserializer. `Refusal_From` exists so that an
overlap question nobody can answer refuses rather than grants, because unknown independence is not
safe parallelism. A key this build cannot account for is the same question one layer down: whether
writing this document back is lossless cannot be established, so it is not written.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:aa70391900fdf30427a57e0b915e7570b439959172f59fd318d5dea77a75895e*

**The guard is at `Load`, and only at `Load`.** That is the single door — `With_Lock`, `Claim`,
`Renew`, `Release`, `Conflicts` and `Validate_Current` all pass through it — and a document that
parsed under `deny_unknown_fields` is by construction one this build accounts for in full, so
`Save` needs no guard of its own and cannot acquire a second, disagreeing one.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:7775124bbe6147178ab530171338c2c69552acae9a9d75705596d4da61eaafe4*

**The schema version explains the refusal and never provides it.** `Load` parses strictly; when
the strict parse fails, and only then, a probe reads `schema_version` out of the text, and a file
newer than this build is reported as `LedgerError::Unrecognized` rather than
`LedgerError::Malformed`. The layering is the point: forgetting to raise `SCHEMA_VERSION` can only
degrade a message, and can never cost a field.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:185ad100e3d205bcd3f7653d8844d8e585e738139265097b5ccf26a3ca09fb67*

**`Save` stamps the version rather than echoing it.** The one state the version cannot explain is
a document carrying keys a build invented while claiming the older number it read: an older reader
then fails the strict parse, probes the version, finds nothing newer than itself, and reports the
file damaged — sending somebody to repair a file that is correct. The experiment below produced
exactly that state, so it is not hypothetical. `schema_version` is therefore the only field `Save`
does not take from its argument.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / The Decision · hash: sha256:5bbf46ac94c40cb2b443cfcb81a346966ea01c39ca472220a01ddc59665edb95*

**`Unrecognized` is its own arm, not a `Malformed`.** The two remedies are opposites: a malformed
ledger is repaired, and this one is left alone while the *reader* is rebuilt. Reporting the second
as the first sends an operator to edit a file that is correct — `OD-LEDGER-009`'s "two causes
wearing one name" with the causes swapped. The CLI maps it to exit `5`: an agent told the ledger
cannot be used at all stops and fetches a person, and a binary that cannot read the board is
exactly that. No new exit code is introduced and README's table does not move.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:a69e01ed011591ec416a69ec40304bd77b8823a28c76601c1bb81b70e798b49e*

## What The Experiment Showed

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:d0d680033ae3a39f925de59aac1ef4058bdc7cbddcf7190f55618f55ea15b75e*

No test in this process can demonstrate that a genuinely older executable is refused: one
`cargo test`, one binary. So the end-to-end case was run by hand, with two real executables, and
this is what was observed rather than what was expected.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:6782511f0d6df76a749f7f251f95b044cd3efcc402d41133eef1eed03b7f0121*

`nomos.exe` was built at `52dbf1a` and copied aside as `stale.exe` before any of this landed. The
change was applied and a second binary built as `fresh.exe`. A copy of the repository's own
`work/ledger.json` was given the shape a `P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER`-era binary will write — one item
carrying a `displaced` entry, and `schema_version` raised to `2` — and both binaries were pointed
at it through `NOMOS_WORK_DIR`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:c7836f72bfa21f1327bd71c000c10c932ed9d1dfed5d8ba5a684f8f334827725*

**`stale.exe work list` exited 0** and printed the whole board, saying nothing about the field it
could not see.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:21e4e951d36617f9e8d057b621ecba19e7a3a324eb33ee9a65ee2b7a2d0024f8*

**`stale.exe work claim` exited 0** and granted the claim. The claim it wrote was correct. Comparing
the file against what it had been handed, one item had lost `displaced` entirely and no other key
set changed. Nothing in the output referred to it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#32

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:4b8cf7bc5495651e9c163463a5c862cb29894b1de3f860159e5816abe2adbc22*

**The version it left behind was `2`.** The old binary echoed the number it read, so the file then
claimed to be a schema this build had never produced while no longer containing the field that
made it one — the state that would have been reported to the *next* old reader as a damaged file.
That is the observation that decided `Save` stamping over echoing, above.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#33

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:6916fbadc3f7a7f1f3404bc7424fede60b6c67f80ca999bf3d960d298f21beba*

**`fresh.exe work list` exited 5**, naming the field and both versions:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#34

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:3eb43915b02f9b40f565d040fea8a21578e101863865836bfcad16a52fa4c12a*

```
this build understands ledger schema 1 and the file is schema 2: unknown field `displaced`,
expected one of `id`, `title`, `why`, `done_when`, `territory`, `state`, `depends_on`,
`blocked`, `claim`, `verification`, `verified`, `abandoned` at line 2964 column 17. Writing it
back would drop what could not be read, so nothing was written. Rebuild (`cargo build -p
nomos-cli`) and retry
```

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#35

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:a5fa07ca857ca1f424779d28f619b39bcdd3a0cef62aae15b2c739f499a3fe2e*

**`fresh.exe work claim` exited 5 and the file was byte-identical afterwards** — same md5 before
and after. That is the pairing the item is about: the same document, one binary that drops a field
and reports success, one that refuses and writes nothing.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#36

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What The Experiment Showed · hash: sha256:1b88b1a281e0e96b0790d0823daa3aae9750dea41a3866690e86c3f7f39b9850*

**The current binary still reads the current board.** `validate`, `list`, `audit` and `show` were
run against the repository's real `work/ledger.json` and all exited 0, with `validate` printing
`ledger is valid (schema 1, and this build understands 1)`. `claim`, `renew` and `abandon` were run
against a copy of it under `NOMOS_WORK_DIR`: all exited 0, no item's key set changed, and the
`"abandoned"` count still equalled the item count. A guard that refused the current file would have
stopped the board rather than protected it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#37

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What This Does Not Reach · hash: sha256:887d210eebe55df22f66b6801b175627d9f4f6ee475040532c3f5ff094cdfdde*

## What This Does Not Reach

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#38

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What This Does Not Reach · hash: sha256:8e467304b4ecb41b4bc7e90334d03060cea0f1928a89251fd42473cd03ef7cd7*

**Binaries that already exist.** A remedy is compiled in. A `nomos.exe` copied last week has none
of this and will go on dropping fields silently until it is replaced. What this decision buys is
that every binary built after it is a safe writer, so the next schema change — `P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER`'s
`displaced`, in the commit after this one — cannot be lost this way. The copies already in flight
are not saved and this record does not claim they are.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#39

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What This Does Not Reach · hash: sha256:b98c8709e7a4fd524c88fdde3e4e2cb166fc81a336764d2950fc8547e41a3a1f*

**The copied-binary workaround is documented, not replaced.** Replacing it means changing how
finishing invokes its predicate, which is `OD-LEDGER-003`'s subject and a different failure mode,
and doing it here would be two decisions in one commit under one record. What this item owed is
that the workaround stops being *silent*, and it does: a copy that has fallen behind now fails at
its first verb with a sentence naming the remedy. README says so where an operator hitting exit 5
will look, and `nomos work validate` reports the file's schema and the build's side by side, so one
command answers "is the executable I copied current?".

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#40

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What This Does Not Reach · hash: sha256:c4ecbb83b4c1c4ba585fc1dcd44eb8d594b31f66d1c7baeffcb6b9ce1cde61ef*

**A file that claims a newer version while containing nothing new is still read.** The version is
not a guard, by decision, so a document whose every key this build declares parses however it is
stamped — and is then re-stamped to what this build understands. That is lossless in data and
visible in the diff. It is stated because it is the exact boundary of what the version does.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#41

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / What This Does Not Reach · hash: sha256:d1a8823e0cca1ab9d5eefc8d0ac1cec5e278740cdf81ef20b2a79e3854780f69*

**The surface snapshot cannot hold this.** Serde attributes are not part of a public API, so
`deny_unknown_fields` moves no line in `tests/contract/surface/nomos-ledger.txt`; the two lines
that move are `SCHEMA_VERSION` and the new error variant. Deleting the guarantee is invisible to
every check in this workspace except the tests written for it. That is why the negative controls
matter more here than usual, and why the completeness test walks the document's shape rather than
naming types: a guard enumerated by hand is only as complete as the hand — `OD-COMPLETENESS-001`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#42

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#43

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Consequences · hash: sha256:48a37dcc9901121cfae9c64a8994a8e3fc1e2531e839d7c0f1b3916e3a3f7818*

A stale session is stopped, not degraded. Every `nomos work` verb exits 5 until its operator
rebuilds, `list` included. That is the intended outcome and it is a cost: an agent mid-item
discovers it at the next verb rather than at the start. Refusing the read-only verbs too is
deliberate — a session allowed to read a document it cannot account for goes on deciding from a
board it is not seeing whole, which is the condition that produced the incident rather than the
write that ended it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#44

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Consequences · hash: sha256:f7b714491a3edf2a7cdfc2268816fc83e0e02b9b4cc9482a8361c6c94a45c294*

Additive schema changes are no longer backward compatible in the read direction. A new build still
reads an old file — every added field carries `serde(default)`, and a document written before
`abandoned` existed is asserted to still load — but an old build no longer reads a new one. That
asymmetry is deliberate and it is the whole trade: forward compatibility for this file was buying
nothing except the ability to lose it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#45

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Consequences · hash: sha256:80d739693f6e066c7e23ee694ab605d18349f3196a57f344925c54192a71d4fa*

A key nobody declared can no longer be parked in the ledger by hand. Adding one now means adding
it to a type.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#46

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Status · hash: sha256:8b1501efecf5aaab88f0940d5804c94111b5c227a27bc5fd9a3e96cca6744236*

## Status

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#47

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Status · hash: sha256:dd465eef60c08ca4bfd8488f844a8c566e9836db0e4db741e04b471894c86c7d*

Accepted. Implemented in `nomos-ledger`, reported by `nomos work validate`, and documented in
README.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-008-a-writer-that-does-not-understand-a-document-must-not-write-it.md#48

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A writer that does not understand a document must not write it back / Status · hash: sha256:92fc6cda056123a01f8c1489d5a3b6cf5f91b1fde1d1dbf4e54972e14ccef639*

Six controls confirmed red, one at a time, each reverted. Removing `deny_unknown_fields` from
`LedgerItem` failed five tests, all of them in this item's own set and no other test in
`nomos-ledger` or `nomos-cli` moving. Removing it from `LedgerDocument`, from `Claim` and from
`Territory` each failed exactly one test —
`Test_Every_Object_In_A_Ledger_Should_Refuse_An_Undeclared_Key`, and nothing else — which is
precisely why that test exists: the three fixtures that carry an undeclared key on an *item* stay
green through all three, so without the shape walk, four of the ten guarded sites could be removed
with the suite still passing. Making `Explain` always answer `Malformed` failed the test that tells
the two causes apart, alone. Making `Save` echo the loaded version failed the test that the stamp
is this build's, alone.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#1
