# A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Question · hash: sha256:52254a5256b6ada57fa87c97c522a19edb2ee43099bccc0efa4fc5e9b557a74c*

`MAXIMUM_LEASE` exists so that an agent which dies holding a claim stops holding territory,
without anybody editing `work/ledger.json` by hand. `item.rs` says so at the definition of
the lapse check.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Question · hash: sha256:60a582d7f297bdde8ce70b0d3586874428af827d5787212d40f12fbbb0c19cb9*

The lease expiring caused exactly what the lease exists to prevent. Document validation
treated `Claimed` with no *active* claim as a violation, and a lapsed lease is precisely
that state. `Save` refuses to persist an invalid document and every claim saves, so the
moment any lease ran out, every claim on the board failed — including claims on items
sharing no territory with the lapsed one. Reproduced by forcing one lease into the past and
then claiming an item with disjoint territory: refused.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Question · hash: sha256:df98fc3b6e46e832173ba510aa242829465bfe71692d52cad157b1a1bde655b3*

The unit level was right the whole time, and that is what hid it. `Has_Active_Claim`
returns false on a lapsed claim, exclusion honours that, and its tests pass. Validation
refused the document before exclusion was ever consulted, so the correct answer never got
to matter.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts · hash: sha256:8b2085acf11be7c20395dc354af67844c69619aa97c3f77d1953a86fa8156986*

## The Decision, In Two Parts

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock · hash: sha256:6aab3e4acc9c45d9f0a49d865e8bb0a40eae128cf8076c13c0b254e9a077a1e7*

### Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock · hash: sha256:a7418237e55d9919bdef266f6d40f59c9c3ba6493774f279dc566bf672936d40*

**A rule that can turn a valid document invalid by the passage of time is not an invariant,
and does not belong in validation.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock · hash: sha256:6347f5b4d8f9b1987b1cad0c94c33336267ac9efadc557f2563e068cb0d2518a*

`Claimed` with a lapsed claim is the normal end of an agent that died. It is what the design
*intends* to happen, and calling it corruption made a file that was written valid stop being
valid on its own, with no writer involved.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock · hash: sha256:08ab76896a33dc0cb53bb1cf400484e1e9586e258e3364ee4a2d83433da8faf5*

What remains is the invariant that cannot move: **an item marked `Claimed` records a claim.**
`claim: None` under `Claimed` is a real corruption — nothing can say whose work it is or was
— and no amount of elapsed time produces it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / Validity is a property of the document, not of the clock · hash: sha256:db0b9e6b68146f03aa30b2f6cb75f1865f02495a68234d725a62921dcfed8eef*

The one time-dependent rule left is `Overlapping_Claims`, and it is safe in the direction
that matters: as leases lapse its violations only ever *disappear*. A document that
validated cannot stop validating. That asymmetry is the test to apply to the next rule
somebody wants to add here.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:dbc431778b258b48ce626a310713572bf4ec33083315a9c822379c23c7da933e*

### A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:80b1ad277b4ac31a567f40d87074ce2ae399bc93c22e8c6a07499202bad9db11*

The other half of the question, and it is settled deliberately rather than left as a
consequence.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:a66d6ab594a90a0402be3ac201d44f95a2c5da04c5e281e4f925ac92017d5a38*

`Has_Lapsed`'s doc comment said a lapse "stops excluding, which is what lets the next agent
take the item". Half of that is true and is what this record restores: it stops excluding
*other* items. The second half was never true — `Claim_Refusal` rejects anything that is not
`Ready` before it ever reaches the lease — and it now stays untrue on purpose.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:2b699f7d08d7dc3db80d6db46013ceded928f825dfe91025e344f7ee539977cd*

`Claim` overwrites `claim`. `claim` is the only thing on a lapsed item recording that the
work was ever started, and `OD-LEDGER-006` decided that must survive: it refused to
synthesize an `Abandonment` for a lapse, because `Abandonment::reason` is *the words the
holder gave* and a lapse has none. So a takeover has nowhere to put the claim it replaces,
and giving it one means reopening what a lapse leaves behind — which is a decision
`OD-LEDGER-006` has already made and this item's scope explicitly does not reopen.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:58e43ee784f610fe6647b4cd4dbfbbc86e5ffebc4a7270ad100b09be7d17fef6*

Taking over a lapsed item is therefore a **different operation from claiming a free one**,
and it does not exist. `P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER` is opened for it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Decision, In Two Parts / A lapsed item stays `Claimed` and nobody else may take it · hash: sha256:9700c8600adf0ccbfd7dabd156bda982bb9bc9a78f51f76d91b03e647cf11262*

*(Amended at version 2. The heading above and the last clause of that sentence are superseded:
"nobody else may take it" and "it does not exist" were true when this record was written and are
not now. `OD-LEDGER-012` supplies the operation this section deferred — `nomos work takeover` —
deciding that the claim it replaces moves to `LedgerItem::displaced` rather than being
overwritten. The first clause is what the answer had to satisfy and it did: `claim` still refuses
a lapsed item, and the one verb that does not refuse it keeps what it displaces. The paragraph
above is kept whole because it is the reasoning that record had to answer, and without it the new
criterion reads as arbitrary. See the amendment note below.)*

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / What A Lapsed Item Looks Like Now · hash: sha256:864ea4e4beba58d53912c5f3cbd8ca0c56ab5cf3b43b3764eff0535dc210e68e*

## What A Lapsed Item Looks Like Now

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / What A Lapsed Item Looks Like Now · hash: sha256:4ab60287162deeac3bbfb2f8390d9bfd0cd87a1dd32660876d46c0c8e8ccd0a4*

`work list` calls it `lapsed` rather than `claimed`. That is the whole of what makes the
deferral above tolerable: an item whose holder is gone reads as work in progress otherwise,
and it is the one state on this board that needs a person. `claimed` was the second word in
this listing to mean something other than what a reader takes it to mean, after `ready` —
see `OD-LEDGER-005`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / What A Lapsed Item Looks Like Now · hash: sha256:bb7ac128202b0fa78a471bdc6f9c9313778d77aa29620f29d3304cb64ca5711f*

The holder's own recovery is unchanged and is now the whole recovery story. `Renew` and
`Release` match on the holder and never took the validating path, so an agent that comes back
can always rescue its own claim. While the board was bricked that was the only recovery
there was; now it is the only thing a lapse blocks rather than the only thing it permits.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / What A Lapsed Item Looks Like Now · hash: sha256:53434c7e1758581db368f3292073d3f9d42764cac607ec08974cc68d00493bfa*

*(Amended at version 2. "The whole recovery story" is superseded — at version 2 it is the cheap
half of one. An agent that comes back renews; an agent that does not is taken over by somebody
who says so. And `lapsed` is no longer the word for the one state on this board that needs a
*person*: it is the word for the one state that needs a *decision*, and it now says a takeover is
available rather than that an editor is. The holder's own recovery is itself unchanged, and the
test that pins it is untouched — it is now also the control on `Take_Over` not having loosened
`Renew`'s holder match. See the amendment note below.)*

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Second Defect: Two Causes Wearing One Name · hash: sha256:f8219332af9caf8d253ff71f554197117777a2cf68df1ac20c6f3bb5269c3ce3*

## The Second Defect: Two Causes Wearing One Name

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Second Defect: Two Causes Wearing One Name · hash: sha256:f0c8effdb22f1a83c0a4d32412ad8ccba1a9b300ba403e6129d01ff28d9a3b97*

`Claim`, `Renew` and `Release` discarded every load and save error and returned
`ClaimRefusal::NoSuchItem`. An unreadable file, a parse error and an invalid document all
told the operator that their identifier matched nothing — sending them to check a spelling
while the ledger was refusing to be written.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Second Defect: Two Causes Wearing One Name · hash: sha256:da797932666e48b7298f9d5dba88ce279c1a5ab7e1313187e8d55d0d1a720a8f*

That is why the defect above needed an experiment rather than a reading, and it is the third
instance of the shape `OD-LEDGER-006` named: a reason destroyed by the failure it explains.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / The Second Defect: Two Causes Wearing One Name · hash: sha256:9a5cd49e200c9e3dcc136b564458c8fd838c2adb789e1cfc16477ac30f70cf85*

`ClaimRefusal::LedgerUnusable` carries what the store said, verbatim, and the CLI maps it to
exit `5` — which the README already defines as "the ledger or its lock could not be used at
all". The distinction between `3` and `5` is the one that repository documents as earning
its own code: an agent told the item is taken picks up something else, and an agent told the
ledger is broken stops and fetches a person. This refusal used to arrive as `4`, after
arriving as the wrong sentence.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:5cb944a4a1301e8ad3517f1765a04a3f16c2d31cb5ec1b14acf903dbfedfe51e*

## Amendment, Version 2

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:22c4702c439df5243e747276bc6e25d6f993f4704e7ea25de5ed0198b943cdb3*

`P10-LAPSE-TAKEOVER` supplies the operation this record deferred, and `OD-LEDGER-012` carries the
decision. This note records what moved.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:87adfa3895fb6f58e149f91b3b4b3839c0a803ab6f62bfb82c164a0949e8bc47*

**Only the second half of one of this record's two decisions moves.** The first decision — that
validity is a property of the document and not of the clock — is untouched, and so is the test to
apply to the next rule anybody wants to add to validation. The second decision was in two parts:
a lapsed item stays `Claimed`, and nobody else may take it. The first part stands, and a takeover
does not change an item's state. The second part is replaced.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:7afc74186f96f05a908d0371a33d76644919b289606b5d7735dfacae2ca9e08b*

**What this record protected is not weakened.** Its stated ground was that `Claim` overwrites
`claim`, that `claim` is the only thing on a lapsed item recording that the work was ever started,
and that a takeover therefore had nowhere to put what it replaces. All three were correct.
`OD-LEDGER-012` answers the third rather than overruling the first two: it gives the takeover
somewhere to put it. `Claim` still does not displace a lapsed holder — a plain `claim` refuses,
now with `ClaimRefusal::Lapsed`, which names the holder it would have displaced and the verb that
does it — and the only operation that does displace one keeps what it displaced.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:59af40ed2990dc53db8e653242e6dca60fcf732f699d013aab0d19ca0a800456*

**This record's title stays literally true.** A lapsed item is still not *claimable*. What exists
now is a different verb, which is exactly the distinction the superseded section drew and then
declined to build.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-009-a-documents-validity-must-not-depend-on-when-it-is-read.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A document's validity must not depend on when it is read, and a lapsed item is not claimable / Amendment, Version 2 · hash: sha256:ad0b6993451aa243324d1c95e27ac1b0fd0b4fe4ebc3a2f08672481cde822425*

**One thing this record got right is worth restating rather than amending.** It settled the
lapsed item's fate deliberately instead of leaving it as a consequence, and named what stood in
the way. That is why the item it opened could be decided on a criterion rather than on whichever
shape was easiest to write — a deferral that records its own reasoning is what makes the next
decision cheap.

# Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:41bc6e4ae345da16c5156f14f0412422a64be34f895cc9875054cbaf217ac176*

The doc comment on `Add` in `crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs` read:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:8ee57adfdff4554845b45cb9985f1ab922971172883107b43e2ec6a7da15c982*

```
/// Records a new item, refusing one whose territory is already spoken for.
```

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:e13708d7d7fca8fb94cdac2a9557fb3ab124602bed012d4608f3a6c254aa6765*

It never did that. `nomos_ledger::Validate` reaches territory through
`Overlapping_Claims`, which begins by filtering the document to items satisfying
`Has_Active_Claim`, and an item arriving at `Add` carries `claim: None` by construction —
`Parse_Add` builds it that way and there is no flag to say otherwise. The comparison
therefore has nothing to say about a new item and has never fired for one. `Add` rejects a
duplicate identifier, appends, and calls `Save`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:014a648e4668b0642838c8bbe19f517c9d2eb92b2b204e4540d1d2b31e1f068e*

The sentence and the function arrived in the same commit, `914a091`, so the claim has been
false for as long as the command has existed.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / Question · hash: sha256:1dcd20a674d9edcf487eb53536348dfc981bf3730ba88b5c88e8b9c3b3286cd1*

It is demonstrated on this board rather than argued from the code. `60d0c5b` and `7efc2a9`
each added an item reserving `crates/substrate/nomos-ledger`,
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store` and `tests/contract` while another session held all three
under a live claim on `P10-SEEDING-SERIALIZES`. Both were accepted. Both are commits
touching `work/ledger.json` and nothing else, which is what an opened item looks like.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:693dde5d5e5b7a4020d09db94231129438cfe7e95f09f2d7da20e2ffbc55be4e*

**The sentence was wrong, not the behaviour. `add` refuses a duplicate identifier and a
document that would not validate, and refuses nothing on account of territory.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:a0fb6c9b764b1b0572990b24b02d2ed89b57001a2e2e78fa7f1fe881899b85ea*

The question is not rhetorical, and answering it "obviously the comment" without stating
why would leave the next reader where this one started. There is a real argument for the
other side: two items on one territory is the condition the ledger exists to detect, and
detecting it earlier is usually better than detecting it later.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:9d3618a411a2d9566d10e6810025b08e6711ac6b6289095564799af47eba995b*

It falls the other way for three reasons, in ascending order of weight.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:52b88b81f78052540c821e94a5362d61f7ab7ae47ed9a00633978c7c95fb6900*

**Opening blocked work is the ordinary case, not the exceptional one.** Both commits above
opened items *because* their territory was held — that is when a defect in the code you are
looking at is noticed. A refusal would forbid the normal way an agent records what it found
while it could not act on it, and the alternative it would push people toward is not
"wait", it is "do not write it down".

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:be41827a3b4cba55ebe39bd65d68733074bed1691f4f2fbafb2741210fe82bde*

**`add` is the door that stays open when the board is closed.** `work/ledger.json` is in
nobody's territory, which is the arrangement that makes `add` available while every item on
the board is held. `OD-LEDGER-007` measured that condition four times in one afternoon —
one claim refusing every other item — and `OD-LEDGER-011` measured 42 of 78 pairs still
blocked by ordinary contention after the serializers were removed. A territory refusal in
`add` would shut the last open door at exactly the moment it is the only one.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:b5e7cec726b240303d1512cf618efa26e1c33035d485e2f060913dace8d3be4d*

**Exclusion belongs where the editing is.** `claim` is the verb an agent runs immediately
before it starts changing files, and it is the verb whose refusal is retryable and carries
the holder's name. `add` writes a sentence about work that may not start for days, against
a board that will have moved by then. A refusal computed at authoring time would be a
statement about a world that no longer exists when the work begins — and it would say
nothing at all about the case it appears to protect against, since two items opened hours
apart on free ground can still be claimed together tomorrow only because `claim` checks
again.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Decision · hash: sha256:ec97e28b193fe3e728e56eb42c247df680f8e6dc2d696752ded8006471acfe9b*

So what `Add` guarantees is smaller than the sentence promised, and the corrected comment
states it exactly: the identifier is unused, and the document that results still satisfies
its own invariants. Validation happens before the write, so an item that would break one
never lands.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Class This Belongs To · hash: sha256:dc9b53c212cbf9106339983bca85fe6eac024903a51e6c391639b9e9fc28065a*

## The Class This Belongs To

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Class This Belongs To · hash: sha256:fefc6baf4c15d70f3639ff7b3d37a0df023ffae564d680e4743bb926b6e33365*

A doc comment asserting a control that does not run is the defect this ledger keeps
recording under other names. `OD-COMPLETENESS-001` is a coverage claim written where nothing
resolves it; `OD-LEDGER-015` is `With_Lock`'s doc comment describing a lock three callers
bypassed. The cost is not the wrong prose. It is that the next person to reason about
whether two items may safely be opened against one territory reads the sentence, is told a
check protects them, and stops looking.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / The Class This Belongs To · hash: sha256:911e0d121007f5e911c85284efdae4d7c0afe5311b3799c579c8187f942039c7*

That is why this is a record and not an edit. The behaviour is unchanged and the diff is a
comment and a test file; what is written down is the reason the guarantee is where it is,
so that "should `add` refuse held territory?" is a question already answered rather than
one re-derived by whoever next notices the gap.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:2d57479d0e31892ffc06d74f76a08ec413915234be5688baf709442eb0124176*

## What Holds It

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:a5877894d0c769c55a22bee26e2347b135603e30b99f90e13dff9207c9cc3b31*

`crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/add_guarantees_what_it_says.rs`, one assertion per clause of
the corrected sentence, driven through the binary for the reason `list_tells_the_truth.rs`
gives — the defect was in what the surface said about the logic, and a caller who is misled
reaches this program through its command line.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:d38606377883d0730a4f1f80ecccfbca0fdf90f9a87a8a8986e64e0981f2fb21*

The accepted case and its deferral are asserted together, because either alone is
misleading:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:2271d395d096258f681c795bf751c98c6b4b997074b40738a49f4072dd3e35e9*

```
$ nomos work claim --item T-1 --holder agent-a
T-1 held by agent-a until unix 1786346963                          (exit 0)
$ nomos work add --item T-2 --territory src/shared.rs
added T-2 reserving 1 path(s)                                      (exit 0)
$ nomos work claim --item T-2 --holder agent-b
refused: T-1 overlaps territory held by agent-a until unix 1786346963
                                                                   (exit 3)
```

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:6f70232209a4b3fc1103eaa539712a6d5338a51c2f869543831cbc8aecbfabc6*

`Test_The_Item_Added_On_Held_Ground_Should_Still_Be_Refused_A_Claim` is the second of those
three lines through to the third. Without it,
`Test_Adding_An_Item_On_Held_Ground_Should_Be_Accepted` reads as a ledger that waves two
agents onto one file — which is the reading the old sentence was written to prevent, and
the reason deleting it alone would not have been enough.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#24

The two clauses that are promised are asserted on their refusals and on the bytes:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:8b99acc1ffc41f5b70377519c8c76a7f84c97b75d976dcd7caf1ece7250cf4b2*

```
$ nomos work add --item T-1 …
T-1 is already on the ledger                                       (exit 4)
$ nomos work add --item T-3 --territory src/c.rs --depends-on T-9
ledger is invalid:
  T-3 depends on T-9, which is not in the ledger                   (exit 1)
$ nomos work add --item T-4 --territory src/d.rs --territory SRC/D.rs
ledger is invalid:
  T-4's territory lists `src/d.rs` and `SRC/D.rs`, which name the same subject; whoever
  wrote it probably believed they were reserving two things        (exit 1)
```

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:27c6468aa7946968f479534f6119b808a4eaa0ed445adb2eafad24a63e854949*

Each refusal is checked against the ledger file read back byte for byte, not against its
item list. A rewrite that happens to preserve the items is still the write `Save` documents
itself as not having performed, and the "validated before the write" clause is about the
write and not about the outcome. Exit 4 rather than 3 for the duplicate is asserted too:
a taken name is not a race somebody wins by waiting, and the exit code is what agents
branch on — `OD-LEDGER-009` records the same distinction being got wrong in `claim`.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What Holds It · hash: sha256:9a3ace8ba1ac87e19d3bcd1459c9f29d6dda6c17a997669b792e379f26d4e6e0*

Two controls stop the set going vacuous. `Test_An_Item_Added_On_Free_Ground_Should_Claim`
moves the territory apart and claims the added item, so the first pair cannot be satisfied
by a ledger that refuses every claim. `Test_A_Well_Formed_Item_Should_Land` adds a valid
item to the same board the two refusals use, so those cannot be satisfied by an `add` that
has stopped accepting anything.

## What This Does Not Hold

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What This Does Not Hold · hash: sha256:84212170921e2804c12dce646814fd568cd2671c448302640919936020a591a6*

**Nothing here goes red if the comment drifts back.** The tests state that the behaviour is
what the corrected sentence describes; they cannot state that the sentence still describes
it. A doc comment is prose, and the only mechanism in this workspace that judges prose
against behaviour is `nomos_rules::mirror`, which resolves the mirror a *declared universe*
names and does not look at free-standing functions.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-010-opening-an-item-on-held-ground-is-how-the-board-is-used.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Opening an item on held ground is how the board is used, so add guarantees a name and a valid document and nothing else / What This Does Not Hold · hash: sha256:9221756d252c2d2511daf4fcc2e33f027d051559de5c4f6836c6ef3f23b7a710*

This is the residue of the class, and it is stated rather than closed. Closing it means
deciding what it would mean for an arbitrary function's doc comment to be checkable, which
is a larger question than the one this item settles and is not obviously answerable at all
— most doc comments describe things no predicate can express. What is bought instead is
cheaper and real: the corrected sentence is true, it is true in a way somebody can run, and
the assertions sit in the same crate as the function, so a reader who distrusts the prose
finds the answer without leaving the directory.

# An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / Question · hash: sha256:262c1a6f4692bd519f7490c61ce3e87d5b8659222a43c4fb8c0870d503120e49*

`OD-LEDGER-007` opened a debt register with two entries, said in terms that it "is expected
to empty", and declined to empty it. `OD-SPEC-007` removed the code coupling behind the
first entry: a canonical record is now registered by its own
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/<ID>.record` file, `governing.rs` is not edited, and
two items writing two different records write two different files. It could not remove the
entry, because the register reads *declared territory* rather than edited files, and twelve
items still reserved the whole crate — authored under `OD-LEDGER-001`'s third rule as it
stood before that record.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / Question · hash: sha256:b936bd263e6b8b5176a325c0de0bab48205fde6d6af0f0940656b1a3b5d51401*

The second entry is the same shape one level up. `P9-PUBLIC-API` checks each crate's public
API into `tests/contract/surface/<crate>.txt`, and an item that widens one crate's API
reserved `tests/contract` entire — twenty-one crates' surfaces plus the whole harness — in
order to write one file inside it. That is `OD-LEDGER-004`'s finding about `docs/records`,
arriving independently and later, and nothing in the mechanism ever prevented the finer
grain: territory is file resolution and `Territory::Intersect` has always compared by
containment.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / Question · hash: sha256:b3b45ac4f71349949cc5fb63e47880d3da8ab75a8039fb8384f28ab803f1d00c*

So this item is a re-authoring pass, not a code change. What made it an item rather than an
edit is that the territories belong to other work, and `P10-SEEDING-SERIALIZES` refused to
narrow somebody else's territory to manufacture a pair — rightly, for that item.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#6

## What Was Measured, And Under Which Projection

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What Was Measured, And Under Which Projection · hash: sha256:75ff81cfe0c5ef978accb80a7b83ef9c46598b81f99cf2f416be0dd45c6fc5a9*

Every figure below is under the **record-writer projection**, which is what
`Record_Writers` in `crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/records_do_not_serialize.rs`
defines: an item that is open, reserves a path under `docs/records`, and has an empty
`depends_on`. Thirteen of the board's items are in it. A parallelism number without its
projection is an unqualified claim, and `OD-SPEC-007` states its own floor the same way.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What Was Measured, And Under Which Projection · hash: sha256:b1c265cf9504ebb0f35292febc21025e5ef6da984063755648828f3d8b94be60*

Two further projections apply and are named because they change the answer:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What Was Measured, And Under Which Projection · hash: sha256:6bb125f3d104eb35b14a535c24a878817b366b00ce0272af2edeeda12fa55822*

* **Claims cleared.** `Unclaimed_Copy` sets every open item back to `Ready` before
  measuring, because the question is whether two items *could* be held at once, not whether
  they happen to be free this second.
* **Constant membership.** `P10-TEST-MASK` finished during this pass. It is excluded from
  all three points below, so that a change in the board's membership is not read as a change
  bought by the re-authoring.

| | pairs | blocked | blocked only by a declared serializer | most holdable at once |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — territories as authored, at `ed8c167` | 78 | **78** | 42 | **1** of 13 |

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What Was Measured, And Under Which Projection · hash: sha256:14966b049b23f052b83a8002b61d366c76b4aef67a305069cb1e878aa2a37040*

Point A is the census the item was opened against and is the line
`Test_A_Run_Should_Report_Whether_The_Board_Is_Parallel` printed on arrival: *13 items, 78

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:47a53fa10f5200ad2077538e3c45dc315cfe72e449b81cbaf8ab7d1b62557345*

**An item reserves the artefact it will write. A snapshot file is an artefact; the snapshot
directory is not. A record's registration file is an artefact; the crate holding it is
not.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:25e06609e5c7a0b0567851634ee161151be00f6ad59842e0f01aeb034f5b99f3*

Twelve unclaimed items were re-authored. Each verdict was re-derived from that item's own
`done_when` against the code at `HEAD` rather than carried over from an earlier pass, which
mattered: the board moved three times while the table was being computed.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:f199caa94fa40fc54a70e4f5292aaf026259065d72a8dac0d48493dd02b1dfcc*

**Eight items gave up `tests/contract`** — every open item that reserved the bare directory.
Seven narrowed to the snapshot files they will write — `surface/nomos-ledger.txt`,
`surface/nomos-contracts.txt`, `surface/nomos-rules.txt`, and so on. One,
`P10-ADD-PROMISE`, gave it up outright: the only
crate it changes is `nomos-cli`, which is the sole entry in `WITHOUT_A_LIBRARY` and has no
snapshot at all, and it adds no test to a corpus-gated file. Reserving the directory bought
it nothing and cost everybody else.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:55b163782d512d7f4780353d21ac7e17698b66e3c17d3b80cc409a20dbd8ca53*

**Twelve items gave up `crates/spec/nomos-spec-store`**, narrowing to
`records/<ID>.record`. This is the larger half and it did not exist as an option before
`OD-SPEC-007` landed: until then, seeding a record was an edit to two shared files in that
crate and the reservation was honest. It is the dividend of that record, collected here.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:0cb5771515bd8d4ac30aa3a118039c7145ed0640b406a823eadfa0fcc808f62b*

**Two items kept a directory, and one that is not a snapshot directory.**
`P10-SPEC-DETERMINISM` genuinely changes the harness — its `done_when` extends the
completeness guard to reach domains that do not construct facts, and that scanner is
`Fact_Domains` in `tests/contract/src/strategies.rs` — so it reserves that file, `src/lib.rs`
where a new export is declared, `tests/determinism_declarations.rs`, and four snapshots. It
does not reserve `tests/contract/src` whole: reading a helper is not writing it, and
`gates.rs` was under a live claim while this ran. The point is accuracy and not a smaller
number, and it is also not a larger one.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:a7def75cf891506e54508375abadfd1930047f245ce5a38cb09b5ad518f3e40d*

**Three under-declarations were repaired**, which is the same defect wearing the other face
and costs concurrency rather than buying it:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:c2a0b80debe48642a85f7f08da8d5896e1a1a021256c82f9d8b91672c2b6f3c9*

* `P10-PATTERN-BRICK` gains `tests/contract/surface/nomos-ledger.txt`. One of the two
  outcomes its `done_when` offers removes `Territory::With_Pattern`, which is exported.
* `P10-REFUSAL-SURFACE` gains `docs/records/OD-LEDGER-001-…md`. Its own `done_when` says
  that if `Conflicts` is removed "the surface snapshot and OD-LEDGER-001 move with it". The
  snapshot was declared; the record was not.
* `P10-RECORD-STEM` gains `work/ledger.json`. Its `done_when` re-authors the open items that
  amend an existing record, which is an edit to that file — the same defect at the file
  every item on the board is edited in that this item's own `why` names. Nothing had ever
  declared it while re-authoring it; this item is the second to do so.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:1cc6eac2b13d7015bb0e794907b9084728cc98fcec1cb7e55a495f6692e02775*

**Only unclaimed items were re-authored.** Two were held while this ran — `P10-TEST-MASK`,
by another session, and this item — and neither was touched. The applying script refuses any
item whose `claim` is non-null and was tested against a board with one held; it also refuses
if an item's territory is neither the recorded before nor the after, which fired repeatedly
and correctly as the board moved underneath it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Decision · hash: sha256:5e4018c7e2a89a2f5c98a102af5c25ca792e77e592c00ca566d20c4013de4b74*

This item did not narrow its own territory while holding it either. It reserved
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store` entire, which stopped being true the minute `OD-SPEC-007`
landed and was blocking `P10-TEST-MASK` over a file this item never touched. It **released
itself unstarted**, was re-authored on the board like everything else, and was claimed again
— the abandonment and its reason are on the item. Narrowing belongs before a claim rather
than during one, and an item whose subject is that rule cannot be the exception to it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / One Widen, Reported Rather Than Netted Out · hash: sha256:21845565d0f15426d6aa0e2e00ee465391e44efdd139eea98814f1d5476da4ea*

## One Widen, Reported Rather Than Netted Out

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / One Widen, Reported Rather Than Netted Out · hash: sha256:ada470bc933142ac445cbba56d07afc6c93f4d373161fbc6e6e6ebd5fa7a5295*

`P10-FACT-BYPASS` was **widened** in the same pass, on the lead's instruction, to add
`crates/host/nomos-cli`. Its `done_when` settles whether a rule consumes facts, and the one
rule signature and its only caller — `crates/host/nomos-cli/src/check.rs` — have to move in
the same commit; no ordering of two items avoids it. Its predicate also omitted
`-p nomos-spec-store` while the item seeds a record, and omitted `--no-fail-fast`, which
undercounts failures. Widening while an item is `Ready` and unclaimed is the sanctioned
order — `4365af6` is the precedent — and once anybody claims it, it is not.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / One Widen, Reported Rather Than Netted Out · hash: sha256:c5d34f84ed1d8dab5cfda98b71c155222a0c706aae05c5f5290f1c58674044c4*

It costs six blocked pairs and one concurrent slot: that is the whole of the difference
between rows B and C above. It is reported as its own row rather than folded into the
narrowings, because a pass that reported only its improvements would be measuring itself.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Defect Found While Closing · hash: sha256:368e6b55370759cb8024a8bd91ae84e0d81aedb7c327fe5e0a4aae814b9579e1*

## The Defect Found While Closing

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Defect Found While Closing · hash: sha256:e1a726cded1dbfeaa9b4a1713abbc8d6c10c88042326a936c37317438b0681ea*

`Test_Every_Declared_Serializer_Should_Still_Serialize` counted with `Paths_Collide`, which
is **symmetric** containment. `tests/contract/surface/nomos-ledger.txt` therefore counted as
reserving `tests/contract`. Measured on this board, under the record-writer projection:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Defect Found While Closing · hash: sha256:b6dedf61a3e66c22b83255a03ad14edc3e76e697ec96c165212d10c0790f076c*

| entry | symmetric, before | symmetric, after | ancestor-or-equal, before | ancestor-or-equal, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crates/spec/nomos-spec-store` | 13 | **13** | 12 | **0** |
| `tests/contract` | 9 | **9** | 8 | **0** |

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Defect Found While Closing · hash: sha256:6438bbd25fbedffe3c631830b9027c123c6ace991e505f65033d6c386eb8428a*

The symmetric column does not move. That is worse than a wrong number: under symmetric
counting **the register can never empty**, because narrowing a reservation never reduces the
count and only deleting the item does — and `OD-LEDGER-007` promises it will empty. The
one entry this item exists to remove was, as written, unremovable by the work that earns it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / The Defect Found While Closing · hash: sha256:fd07795ea586b48930f1b2bf769bca9231b977a4cdc73d262a01cc56bcecae77*

The repair is one line and it is a direction, not a new comparison: count a writer only when
it reserves the declared path **or an ancestor of it**. `Covers` takes that direction from
the collision rather than deciding containment a second time beside `Territory::Intersect` —
if two paths collide under this ledger's rule then one contains the other, and the shorter
normalized spelling is the container, which is the tie-break `Shared_Paths` already used to
name the broader of two paths.

A related finding, smaller: `tests/contract` was never a *universal* reservation even under
the old authoring. `P10-LOCK-BYPASS` reserved nothing beneath it, so

The same symmetric comparison appears in `Undeclared_Serializers` and is deliberately left
there. Its failure mode is the opposite one — it over-reports, and a guard whose instruction
is "declare this or remove the coupling" errs safely by over-reporting. Changing two
directions in one commit with a control for only one of them is not a thing this file should
do.

## What The Guard Proves, Rather Than The Author Asserting It

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#35

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Guard Proves, Rather Than The Author Asserting It · hash: sha256:3a5ad393cf5252ff05ff5a1e47af89c1c29f069367b1eaf464937e1a55c7ff19*

`Test_Two_Items_Widening_Different_Crates_Should_Be_Held_At_Once` derives a pair of open
record writers that reserve *different* crates' snapshot files and are otherwise
territorially independent, and claims both through the real ledger against a copy of the
real board. Derived and not named: two identifiers written into a test would be right until
one of them finished, which is precisely how `OD-LEDGER-007`'s predecessor died.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#36

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Guard Proves, Rather Than The Author Asserting It · hash: sha256:bcd8df822d1279cc0a67e3577ff49446f3f0005b743db78c7b0e1f26a9a714b4*

Stated over the whole territory rather than over a projection, unlike
`Test_A_Record_Should_Exclude_Nobody_But_Its_Own_Writer`. That test has to project because
two record writers genuinely do share code; here the pair is required to be independent
outright, because a snapshot grain that works only once the rest is ignored buys nobody a
concurrent claim.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#37

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Guard Proves, Rather Than The Author Asserting It · hash: sha256:8af613cfc9ada417a0dc85f17624e231988b4332df1f0adad408a5dbdf19051e*

Its control, `Test_Restoring_The_Snapshot_Directory_Should_Refuse_The_Pair`, puts one of the
pair back on the bare `tests/contract` and asserts the other is refused **by name**. Both
were also confirmed red against the pre-re-authoring board: with the empty register and the
old territories, the acceptance test fails reporting that no such pair exists and
`Test_Every_Universal_Reservation_Should_Be_Declared` fails naming
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store`. Removing a register entry early reddens the universal test;
removing it late is what the staleness test is for; and the only commit in which both are
green is the one that does the re-authoring and the removal together.

## What The Census Cannot See

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#48

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Census Cannot See · hash: sha256:3527a17623ca214d035b198f875d82882bbc2227fcb54659faaa0be4f6b3c8a4*

`Record_Writers` excludes any item with a non-empty `depends_on`, and it is right to: an
unmet dependency refuses a claim for reasons that have nothing to do with territory, and
every assertion in that file would fail for the wrong reason. The consequence is that **a
dependent record writer's serialization is invisible to the guard that exists to measure
it.** A dependent item can reserve `tests/contract` entire, serialize every claim on the
board against it, and appear in none of the numbers above — the pair count, the register's
staleness, and the search for an undeclared universal reservation all look past it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#49

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Census Cannot See · hash: sha256:59778207babdfecb870b11e3e29014e74178b725869112faf32c5d8b1295376c*

`P9-AUTHORING` was exactly that while it was open, and no figure in `OD-LEDGER-007` or in
this record ever counted it.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#50

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What The Census Cannot See · hash: sha256:6eefb610a5926ae57dcf454960626e9856aa7900846bb4f33afdfae54e3db951*

This is stated and not fixed here. Fixing it means deciding what the census should say about
an item that cannot be claimed today for a reason other than territory, and that is a
different question from the one this item settles. It is also not repairable by widening this
item's territory, since the exclusion is a line in a test file this item already holds and
the difficulty is the meaning rather than the reach.

## What This Costs

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#52

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What This Costs · hash: sha256:8ae7afa8697e5c85c3cd042d6da0d64f18db1766d598282dad7e4b75fb250ddc*

The debt register is empty. `KNOWN_SERIALIZERS` is `&[]`, which makes
`Test_Every_Declared_Serializer_Should_Still_Serialize` vacuous — it iterates nothing — and
that is the intended terminal state rather than a hole. The register is the *declared* half
of the pair `OD-LEDGER-007` set up; the derived half,
`Test_Every_Universal_Reservation_Should_Be_Declared`, is unchanged, still runs against the
real board, still has its own control, and is what fails when a third structural serializer
arrives. A declaration that makes growth a decision has to be able to start from nothing.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#53

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What This Costs · hash: sha256:308904c1e72bd19b5b25f11df277a55eb5723110559cbdf893b0ba8474cf2e0b*

Forty-two of the seventy-eight pairs are still blocked, and every one of them is now ordinary
contention: two items that want the same crate, which is what territory is for and which
resolves when one of them finishes. Nought are blocked by a rule that will not resolve. That
distinction is the whole of what `OD-LEDGER-007` built the register to make, and this is the
first run on which the second number is zero.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#54

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What This Costs · hash: sha256:90fefea24ededdfe8de405e5eda3ef469a9d18a08469c14af240cf3ef65ab0dd*

Those seventy-eight pairs count this item, which is a record writer while it is open. It
finishes in this commit, so the line the next run prints is *12 items, 66 pair(s), 36
blocked, 0 of those only by a declared serializer* — the same board, one writer fewer. Both
figures are under the record-writer projection; neither is comparable to a run on a board
with different membership, which is why the table above holds membership constant.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-011-an-item-reserves-the-snapshot-it-writes-and-the-register-empties.md#55

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: An item reserves the snapshot file it writes, and the debt register empties / What This Costs · hash: sha256:157a8de3a9930a42cbbe5883cef2371cc6d6b57fefb0e136220357f413fb9812*

What is not bought: the finer grain is a property of what the items *say*, and nothing stops
the next item from being authored at `tests/contract` again. `OD-LEDGER-001`'s third rule is
what would have to change to prevent it, and the two guards here are what would notice.

# A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / Question · hash: sha256:cfdd429fd90281aaae5ac09ae0298344c7bcf861f12dcaca3e1909eb33a655dd*

`MAXIMUM_LEASE` exists so that an agent which died holding a claim stops holding territory
without anybody editing `work/ledger.json` by hand. For every item except the one it died on,
that is what happens. For that one item it is not.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / Question · hash: sha256:daec4e7aaecc687535dcc2ecd06bec25a0ba2e56bd185a16e1dcd55bc26484db*

`Claim_Refusal` rejected any state that is not `Ready` before it consulted the lease. `Renew`
and `Release` match on the holder, and the holder of a lapsed claim is by definition a process
that died — that is the only way a lease lapses on its own. The item was unreachable by
anybody until a person edited the file, which is the outcome the lease was introduced to make
impossible.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / Question · hash: sha256:94391785793cd3e02a76999cf9118049d02a798a897fa6051c0761abd8c885df*

`OD-LEDGER-009` settled that deliberately rather than leaving it as a consequence, and named
what stood in the way: `Claim` overwrites `claim`, `claim` is the only thing on a lapsed item
recording that the work was ever started, and `OD-LEDGER-006` decided that must survive. A
takeover had nowhere to put the claim it replaces.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / Question · hash: sha256:4156dfc0b71f10ff941ec16af795e30af84a13bd16deb01fdcc538aae7cb06dc*

So this record is not about whether a lapsed item should be recoverable. It is about where the
claim goes.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / The Criterion · hash: sha256:f6e9dccf97880153d621eae5bb695064134fac00ebf66b32eae2c574090b2d77*

## The Criterion

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / The Criterion · hash: sha256:64e141c9372d98229fc1e32f027a25fd1fbe4fd37f04d45098b617cb717a67f8*

`OD-LEDGER-006` refused to synthesize an `Abandonment` for a lapse because
`Abandonment::reason` is *the words the holder gave* and a lapse has none. The rule underneath
that refusal is the one applied here:

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / The Criterion · hash: sha256:da6a8069239098c2d37faa98d460184c844e36243de0933e6e1fa868bf380a52*

**What survives a transition is what somebody actually knew at the time.**

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / The Criterion · hash: sha256:c6c10731741a3b3e190b9877798e9de09145d649fc2d364a770d8363a8de698c*

A lapse knows who held the item, when they took it, and when the lease ran out. It does not
know why they stopped. A record of a lapse therefore carries the first three and has no field
for the fourth — not an empty one, not a filled-in one. There is nothing to invent because
there is nowhere to put an invention.

### docs/records/OD-LEDGER-012-a-lapse-is-taken-over-and-the-claim-it-replaces-is-kept.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A lapse is taken over by a verb of its own, and the claim it replaces is kept / The Criterion · hash: sha256:80f9704b12b8afed2a9223f06311e186d802fa7d4602bc09bcf610e01e68fe83*

That criterion decides the three shapes this item was opened with. A synthesized
`Abandonment` is refused, unchanged: `work show` prints an abandonment as `abandoned by X at
unix N: <reason>`, and a manufactured "the lease expired" would read on that surface as a
sentence the dead agent typed. Filler wearing a record's clothes, which this repository
refuses elsewhere for placeholder records.
