*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Question · hash: sha256:7c7b2ab594bd01918db2e5858e3141cdf4e5166e0a6448d5d2287e997bc3cae1*

The objection is correct. It is also narrower than it looks.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:abe8768e0b2e50ac65b62bd810bc952e39085500266efdeb7df4d4c606a1494b*

## Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:222cce0652dd1f43092fdb27b1e8201f07731ba57e853d9739fc1d49a68213de*

`OD-LEDGER-007` §"Why The Structural Remedy Is Not Applied Here" refuses one specific
derivation: one whose **input is `docs/records`**. That is fatal to the derivation it names
and to no other. What makes the guard a check is not that its second side is hand-typed into
one file — it is that the second side is **authored independently of the directory it is
compared against**.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:f27b3b7388a2f0b2882b612abbee57e18d7c929cb1ea2c80816c78e93eff21de*

So the second side stays authored, and stops being one file.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:4287d263b9f92d33d975509d87c20bf9e5e01e0d6cefef034aa28e8e9b0f57be*

A record becomes governing by having a registration under
`crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/`, one file per record, named for the identifier:

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:f319d624dd6c00a7f107ce1a4a7a651c8d7a5efb8c31119de6348836b57229d8*

```
# The registration for OD-LEDGER-007. Writing the record file does not make a record
# governing; this file does.
path: docs/records/OD-LEDGER-007-a-record-excludes-nobody-and-two-other-files-serialize-the-board.md
```

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:43371b4858ce847712dfa3c0a213e2b0ddd526402efa3f7fc99b6ac24a221046*

The identifier is the file stem and appears nowhere inside it, because an `id:` key would be
a second place for the identity to be wrong. The body names the path, because a slug is not
derivable from an identifier and renaming one should touch that record's own registration and
nothing else.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:b17c2fc9801788feddea368b8dcad4d6c545c7f3eef3a9a47126e5fb11d97c62*

A build script reads that directory — **and only that directory** — and generates the two
tables into `OUT_DIR`. `docs/records` is never enumerated by anything that produces
`GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS`; the repository root reaches the generator only so that a registration
naming a file that is not there can be refused.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:d052c928e80111a1a2fffdcc17489a9a365d9c2499009c41f522c4eebb122603*

The guard's two sides are therefore what they always were. Side A is every file under
`docs/records` declaring `authority: canonical-normative-record`. Side B is a set a human
wrote down. The author still performs two independent acts, and forgetting the second is
still what the guard catches: writing `docs/records/OD-STORE-001-….md` and not writing
`records/OD-STORE-001.record` puts the identifier on side A and not on side B, and `unseeded`
is non-empty. `OD-SPEC-005`'s six records would fail today exactly as they failed then.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:175541938b74141d0af2aefddc345893edcd2febbd7c0192328524818daa5288*

What changes is the *locality* of the declaration, not its independence. That is the whole of
the trade, and it is the point: two record writers now write two different files, so a record
excludes nobody but its own writer — in the store as well as in `docs/records`, which is what
`P10-RECORD-LOCK` bought one level down and `OD-LEDGER-007` found defeated one level up.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Answering The Vacuity Objection Directly · hash: sha256:2549b68f736e26586695270ff470689266ed651928e58c11631b8c1535bb96ea*

There is one thing this arrangement cannot prove about itself, and it is written here rather
than left to be discovered. No test in a consistent tree can detect a later "simplification"
of the build script into globbing `docs/records`, because in a consistent tree the two
directories yield the same identifiers and every assertion still passes. What guards it is
structural — the reader takes its directory as a parameter, and
`Test_The_Reader_Should_Enumerate_The_Directory_It_Is_Given` hands it a directory of one
while the repository holds thirty-two — plus a textual check over the call sites,
`Test_The_Build_Script_Should_Not_Enumerate_The_Record_Directory`. That check says in its own
doc comment that it is textual and is not evidence about behaviour. A textual check is a
textual check, and calling it more than that would be the same overclaim this record is
about.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand · hash: sha256:2acaa5baea1a84731533c69d4589c134e431442cf4a29180837633bebd7dd528*

## Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand · hash: sha256:9350011e6cdac20e60d3fb9ef12997985e4ec51c3df771ff014ce43dff7c8460*

`RECORDS` and `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS` keep their `const` items in `governing.rs` verbatim.
Only the initializers become `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))`.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand · hash: sha256:fe30e3142d02d0585cd97862d2364f6b8a19fd9c59ebea09e93780e6349d2881*

This is load-bearing and it was settled by running the real scanner rather than by reading
it. `nomos_rules::Universes_In` matches `syn::Item::Const` with a slice type and public
visibility and **never inspects the initializer**, so an `include!` in initializer position
produces a `DeclaredUniverse` identical to the literal slice's — same path, same name, same
`kind: Constant`, same claimed mirror — and `tests/contract` needs no change at all, snapshot
included. An `include!` at *item* position is `syn::Item::Macro` and is dropped: the universe
returns **zero** rows, `Test_The_Declared_Table_Should_Match_What_Is_Derived` reports the row
as vanished, and deleting that row to make it green would leave the workspace's most-cited
declared universe uncounted forever. The same probe showed a `static` is not recognised
either.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand · hash: sha256:49b126da0dced36c38e289121759a1fd648b67ea48978a8b2e7ec4a5b60ecc5c*

The generated fragments are bare `&[…]` expressions, which the scanner reports `Unparseable`
rather than empty, and `Check_Completeness_Mirrors` turns `Unparseable` into a finding. So
they go to `OUT_DIR` and never into `src/`.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Why The Declaration Site Stays Written By Hand · hash: sha256:525cea1e0a7a82573742907db7ed0587df3d5ac938d1a8c5dab0ea54e5b00dad*

The prediction held: `tests/contract/surface/nomos-spec-store.txt` and
`tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes.rs` are byte-for-byte unchanged, and this item
reserved neither. One thing the probe could not have predicted was found by compiling, and it
is recorded here because the next person to hit it will lose an hour. `Without_Test_Modules`
in `tests/contract/src/gates.rs` blanks from a `#[cfg(test)]` marker to the **next** brace
block in the file, whatever that block happens to be. `#[cfg(test)] mod registration;` carries
no braces, so placed among the other `mod` lines in `lib.rs` it swallowed
`pub use authoring::{…}`, and `Test_Every_Crates_Public_Surface_Should_Match_Its_Snapshot`
reported eleven exports missing and a re-export it could not resolve — a snapshot failure with
no relation to anything this item changed. The declaration was moved to the end of `lib.rs`,
where nothing braced follows it, with a comment saying why. That is a workaround at the call
site, not a fix: the scanner is wrong for any crate that puts a brace-less `#[cfg(test)]` item
above a braced one, and `tests/contract` was outside this item's territory.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What The Literal Count Was Buying · hash: sha256:ee599c4b8b992c5713d397c531c95c0b240766594fff6821fca9f5b84c742534*

## What The Literal Count Was Buying

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What The Literal Count Was Buying · hash: sha256:012916e2844cda1c8d56d59697436822cf4557a86ea82471b4181f3f179211de*

`assert_eq!(GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS.len(), 31)` was the last file forcing every record writer
into one crate, and it was not decoration. It bought two things, and they are not the same
thing.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What The Literal Count Was Buying · hash: sha256:955388ad72eb8012e951e906b83a6357d76e15e8fce17ee7e655f2581848ee1a*

**The deliberate step.** `OD-SPEC-005` and `OD-LEDGER-001` both describe raising it as the
cost adding a governing record is meant to carry. That cost is exactly what this item exists
to remove, and removing it is not a loss: the deliberate step survives as the registration
file. It is still a separate artifact, still authored by hand, still visible in the diff as a
file somebody added. It is no longer *shared*, which was never part of what it bought — that
was a side effect of where it happened to live.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What The Literal Count Was Buying · hash: sha256:3d9d08edc424b77560d485a72a1b55b3ee07437e7076994c9edd211a30db11a8*

**The coordinated deletion.** This is the real one. A record file and its declaration deleted
*together* pass both directions of `Test_Every_Canonical_Record_On_Disk_Should_Be_Governing`,
because the two sets still agree — they agree about a record that is gone. Nothing else in
this workspace sees that. The literal count saw it, and it is worth being precise about how:
it saw it by requiring the deleter to remember a **third** artifact. It worked by
forgetfulness, not by derivation.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What The Literal Count Was Buying · hash: sha256:b002dcb52eb868ec3a562f54ebff8d6064d14334632e761668755a28421837bb*

No derived count can replace it. A count derived from the registrations falls when a
registration is deleted; a count derived from `docs/records` falls when a record is deleted;
neither notices when both fall together. The only thing that can notice is an artifact
outside both — which is what the literal was.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Decision · hash: sha256:dc9e9d8ab6528b7b308fc1f23d52ff0ff2e814a01e253bb619d66ed8045833b1*

## The Decision

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Decision · hash: sha256:e3b08473602ee2c063b5a8294ce25438184fb49ed44b22ea5232bce536de6125*

**A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor.**

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: code · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Decision · hash: sha256:bf0a456e04f1fb2a4b31dadfa8e0abfef6c192a7aa5f83e12e40bfc56edc1174*

```rust
const FEWEST_GOVERNING_RECORDS: usize = 32;

assert!(GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS.len() >= FEWEST_GOVERNING_RECORDS, "…");
```

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Decision · hash: sha256:4b7c3123b3589f67e6180eda6dfb0d06d66f8efcf2122cb796b85c6c52cf6025*

The floor keeps the coordinated-deletion guarantee by exactly the mechanism the literal used:
a deletion has to be accompanied by lowering it, and a deleter who forgets goes red. It gives
up the ceiling. Adding a record no longer costs an edit to this file — which is the item —
and adding one is no longer visible here at all.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Decision · hash: sha256:8bd4189fbe8c8267a7dc20822235bf2f1af7fa5e0bcf3a8ecc6eac15846e3bda*

The floor is a third artifact for the same reason the literal was, and it is *not* raised on
addition. It is lowered by a deliberate removal, and it may be raised for free by any item
that already has this file open for another reason.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:50e8d3d1d6c4a24186d6e6a0bd26f4a9d0b928104cf0c665f864e60eda7c8cd4*

## What This Costs

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#32

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:611f3e555aabf9fb2484daeb07d1ee6ef17cda89b8d3bc985cc9e7021b535805*

**Drift.** The floor's guarantee is exact only while the count sits on it. Once the count has
risen above, a coordinated deletion inside the slack is caught by nothing here. The literal
had no slack. This is the one guarantee that is genuinely weaker after this change, it is
weaker by an amount equal to the distance between the count and the floor, and nothing forces
that distance to close. A record deleted from a workspace of sixty, with the floor still at
thirty-two, is a deletion this workspace will not notice.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#33

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:ae4a10ed657b9b0b7591b7a684676d509cc96ba28461b77fda6d2d30b1cbc1fd*

The alternative considered was an upper bound as well — a declared slack, failing when the
count exceeds the floor by more than some number. It was rejected: it reintroduces the shared
edit on an unpredictable schedule, so instead of every record writer colliding, one
unforeseeable record writer in every N collides with all the others. A rule that fires
unpredictably is worse to author against than one that fires always.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#34

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:bd9c3e835772126a5dd08eaaef616d1c31a8f481851f39ce807e9628e89d0036*

**One assertion narrows.** `Test_The_Records_Should_Be_Present_As_Disposed_Content` compares
`count(source_documents)` against `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS.len()`. That incidentally caught
`RECORDS` and `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS` disagreeing, because they were two lists kept by hand —
and they had already drifted in one respect: the two lists were in different orders,
`OD-LEDGER-001` and `OD-SPEC-004` transposed between them, harmlessly because both are sets.
They are now generated from one input and cannot disagree at all. The second subject becomes
impossible by construction rather than checked, which is stronger, and the assertion keeps the
subject its message actually claims. The remaining hazard, two registrations naming one
document, is a refusal in the reader rather than a test. Its doc comment says so, because
leaving the old one would have been an overclaim.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#35

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:c64cffc0320b9b7f1cca51e3f40c738b02a5afbef4485fe1b5e63898b348e62a*

**A build script.** `nomos-spec-store` acquires one, and code that used to be read by rustc is
now written by a program. It has no dependencies and must keep none, its reader is under unit
test including every one of its refusals, and it refuses rather than skips on all of them — a
registration skipped instead of refused is a governing record that quietly stops governing,
which is `OD-SPEC-005`'s defect wearing a build script's clothes. The reader lives in
`src/registration.rs` and is reached from `build.rs` by `#[path]` rather than copied, because
two readers of one format are two answers waiting to disagree — which this workspace has
written down twice already.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#36

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:bac942ea8c8f534883a872b125becb34204a0fe4f1c40f1ac7a09669471ff815*

**The register does not empty today.** `OD-LEDGER-007`'s `KNOWN_SERIALIZERS` reads declared
territory, not edited files, and twelve open items were authored under `OD-LEDGER-001`'s rule
as it stood. Removing the entry in the commit that dissolves the coupling would redden
`Test_Every_Universal_Reservation_Should_Be_Declared`, because those twelve territories still
reserve the crate. The entry stays and its *reason* is restated: it no longer describes a rule
that binds new items, it describes twelve territories authored before this record, and it
comes out when the last of them is finished or re-authored. A register that over-reports is as
useless as one that under-reports, and the reason is the part that would have been false.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#37

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / What This Costs · hash: sha256:d352bbd3b6b4c2308270e31974ddbad055b72e6e42a31723f84fbc15a6bf3e52*

Measured on the board the day this was decided: twelve open record writers, sixty-six pairs,
sixty-six blocked, forty-five of them by nothing but the two declared serializers, and twelve
by nothing but this crate. Those twelve are what this buys, once the reservations follow it
out. The other thirty-three are held by `tests/contract` as well and are not this record's
subject.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#38

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:9d29c689787b10c075a20d1bc371fd706f9b84455ca7605e4074019973330315*

## The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#39

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:e5c049e0c2c78a401a2183cc194223068f61579eee3521f1d28e8479712e26fa*

Every control below was observed failing before it was relied on, in the manner `OD-SPEC-005`
recorded its three.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#40

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:b699ebe05d360e5b064f870fb435dab1b31966b72e84c494570427b39187f356*

**The guard did not go vacuous.** `Test_A_Record_Whose_Registration_Is_Missing_Should_Be_Unseeded`
runs the real comparison with the real canonical set and the governing set minus one element
and asserts the missing identifier is reported. `Test_A_Registration_With_No_Record_Should_Be_A_Phantom`
is the other direction. Both call the same extracted `Disagreements` the assertion calls, so a
control claiming the guard would have caught something is exercising the guard rather than a
copy written beside it.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#41

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:687101c608bb4550b6003dba8f9ec84b3b5b4743c78a3cc47fc7072c478483ca*

**Side B is the registration directory.** `Test_The_Governing_List_Should_Be_The_Registration_Directory`
reads the `.record` stems at test time and compares them against `GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS`, with
its own vacuity guard.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#42

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:b3fc9739dc05f349e57c0407abbc65303b3c03b2a72b468002288808854e61bf*

**The refused derivation, exhibited.** `Test_Comparing_The_Directory_Against_Itself_Would_Check_Nothing`
performs the comparison `OD-LEDGER-007` declined — both sides from `docs/records`, including a
record nobody registered — and asserts it comes back clean. It asserts nothing about the
arrangement in place. It exists so the next person to propose globbing `docs/records` finds a
test that already says what would happen.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#43

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:bff306d960ff75c716a9b1704ebb9b753cf261b637e619e3ac8b67d2e3875a00*

**The reader refuses rather than skips**, on a missing directory, an empty one, a file that is
not a registration, a stem that is not an identifier, a body with no `path:` line, one with
two, an unknown key, a path outside `docs/records`, a path that is not on disk, and two
registrations naming one record. Each is a unit test asserting `Err` and not a short `Ok`.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#44

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:8367e18179656a12312006407ea2be59be6452d0a0d25123b583a490891ffd65*

**The control that cannot be a test.** Deleting a registration file and watching
`GOVERNING_RECORD_IDS` shrink requires a rebuild, and no `#[test]` causes one. It was run
twice by hand and both results are written down here rather than asserted by something that
did not do them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#45

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:ce04a301dae7f28403197b773507094074a1382bc6955846e02f8dab9bd3d4f4*

*Registration removed, record left on disk.* `records/OD-GATE-001.record` was removed and
`cargo test -p nomos-spec-store --test governing_records_are_present --no-fail-fast` run: 12
passed, 4 failed. `Test_Every_Canonical_Record_On_Disk_Should_Be_Governing` failed naming
`OD-GATE-001` as unseeded — **this is the proof the guard did not go vacuous** — and
`Test_Every_Governing_Record_Should_Resolve_By_Id` failed on the floor at 31 against 32. The
two set-level controls failed as collateral, which is what they should do in a tree whose two
sides disagree. `Test_The_Governing_List_Should_Be_The_Registration_Directory` stayed green,
correctly: both it and the generated list lost the entry together. The file was restored and
the suite returned to green.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#46

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / The Controls, And The One That Is Not A Test · hash: sha256:ddb12ade23eb5af3e7bdd65a0bdc77c84309cba87d2d7d674d6467aa6ded60cc*

*Record and registration removed together.* Both `docs/records/OD-GATE-001-….md` and
`records/OD-GATE-001.record` were removed: 15 passed, **1 failed**. Every other assertion in
the file passed, including *both directions* of
`Test_Every_Canonical_Record_On_Disk_Should_Be_Governing` and
`Test_The_Governing_List_Should_Be_The_Registration_Directory` — because the sets agree about
a record that is gone. Only the floor failed. That is the "What The Literal Count Was Buying"
section demonstrated rather than argued, and it is the reason the floor exists. Both files
were restored.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#47

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Status · hash: sha256:8b1501efecf5aaab88f0940d5804c94111b5c227a27bc5fd9a3e96cca6744236*

## Status

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-007-a-record-is-registered-by-its-own-file-and-the-count-becomes-a-floor.md#48

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A record is registered by its own file, and the count assertion becomes a floor / Status · hash: sha256:60d6c434d33b9bee4f729cf58b6a3f932d485b90e0ba180daf5265dc947a8973*

Closed by `P10-SEED-GRAIN`. `OD-LEDGER-001` is amended at version 4: an item that will write a
canonical record claims its record identifier and its own registration file, and no longer the
store's governing list.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#1

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections · hash: sha256:be3f32aa8b961bfc034ab00fab8f482040b86951b658f02fc67e02134057bca9*

# Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Question · hash: sha256:aeb31fd91d39f0d3076e358be881aa671aa024a2d20d43bd0e717be897566071*

A typed layer of `FeatureRequest`, `DesignSpec` and `FeatureResult` cannot be started until
one thing is recorded, because the answer is the schema written down. Authored files with
typed front matter and a derived store index is a different schema from structured records
whose markdown is generated, and the difference reaches every row.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Question · hash: sha256:1927763af9bae79dcd78a020afa0e9fb6848a0147500b2dc9b6689e4529b15c7*

An earlier attempt on this item reached the opposite answer to the one below, on the
evidence available then. It is worth saying why that answer is not simply overturned by
preference.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:d734747d67d2b9d8c065dfb0059fe3f532d4eb8a7d4504b242c3bfaed443d12d*

## What A Feature Request Is

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:a523790ed99689796607757f95eb93eb047e3074d6fd2420e0ab6cc92af62abd*

Naming this first, because the substrate question cannot be answered about an object nobody
has defined, and because this repository already has two things a reader will confuse it
with.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:663ccfeeed45012da7fbb217c7ad4b7ccfb0bcef1329de6dfaf0443f78b3bf4f*

A **feature request** is a structured submission recording what somebody asked for, before
anybody has decided how or whether to answer it. It carries the intent, the goal, the
behaviour wanted, how the asker will know it worked, and what must not break. It carries
what was asked separately from what was later clarified, and it names the decisions it needs
that nobody has taken yet.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:9c8e7198d07e3adcb48a0bfc2ca8499aaa0a174b811a8027ca32240470f13e94*

It is **not a work item**. `work/ledger.json` holds items, and an item reserves territory, is
claimed by exactly one holder, and is refused if it reserves nothing. A feature request
reserves nothing, is held by nobody, and may produce many items or none.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:707cf0211b648bfe352ec4c2b14ddfa2e7c32622058310382d3f420ec62ff0b3*

It is **not a decision record**. A record argues a case and the argument is the artifact. A
feature request makes no argument; it states a want and the constraints on satisfying it.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:ed843189b873a69f4485f9297f0d3aaf5d74c03ab73c85125f3547179f4fe860*

A **design specification** is the answer to a feature request that has been chosen: the
alternatives considered, the one selected, the architecture delta, and what acceptance will
require. A **feature result** is what was actually built against that design, including where
it deviated and what it left owed.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What A Feature Request Is · hash: sha256:0eebe60fd18132e5cc455279e9f78473f303ccecc816bf92b4eab555c4f52498*

The three are one lifecycle and are decided together here, because splitting them across
substrates would put the split in the schema of every row that joins them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Decision · hash: sha256:bb911b57471cf549b321ed51767a1a0fa2223cf538d71fc33438bd6229d08533*

Feature requests, design specifications and feature results are **born structured**. The
canonical form of each is the structured record. Every markdown, YAML, JSON and HTML document
about them is a projection, and no such document is authored by hand.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Decision · hash: sha256:9fe26149c8e5c3fcdf4bdc135d53705522d1a24abe14431b6a1106112f3b5382*

This is `ARC-SPECDB-002` applied rather than a new rule. That record decides the axis: an
object is born structured when its schema can be stated before its content exists. These
three pass that test unambiguously. The questions a feature request answers — what do you
want, why, what should happen, how will you know it worked, what must it not break — exist
before any particular request does. They can be written as a form, and a form written in
advance is exactly what the test asks for.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Decision · hash: sha256:f4e93e720fb406823b20a611844b2083911cccd392bbf6b28e69aa2f417f7a4a*

Governing records fail the same test and stay document-first, which is why this decision does
not disturb them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken · hash: sha256:60a211f21565e58d219b004010cd06f6f7ad7dcb51107c6465fe31be89906118*

## Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken · hash: sha256:03c1ec7e5f60e6cb5deabaed613b4e7ec7aedc0aa56efa451fcbc407a1bc0a25*

The earlier answer — an authored file under `docs/records` with typed front matter, and the
store as a derived index — rested on three grounds. Two of them have moved.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken · hash: sha256:661f55c21d5023f543bdc7348c193f86696235a91d09653871189c5300a87f0a*

The first was that nothing persists a specification database, so what survives an invocation
is the file. That is still true of the build and is not an argument about these objects.
`SpecificationStore::Open` exists and is called by nothing; the only construction site in the
host is `In_Memory`. The store is not durable because nothing needed it to be, and this
decision is the thing that needs it. A fact about what has been wired is weak evidence about
what should be.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken · hash: sha256:ee572b4890cf69d58f91001a8729a77ddd81e82bc63ab958d5f6f2c30d94bd08*

The second was that deciding per artifact would put two substrates in one build and encode
the split in every typed row. That objection is correct and `ARC-SPECDB-002` was written to
answer it. It is fatal to a split drawn on artifact kind. The split taken here is drawn on a
property of the objects, is stated as a rule that applies to objects nobody has proposed yet,
and is therefore not the failure that objection describes.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#20

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Why The Authored-File Answer Is Not Taken · hash: sha256:aa3af1823e881294ba4fd627580f059b3540c6cf6287f569784132814299b298*

The third ground was that the price of the store option was out of date in the buyer's
favour. That one held up, and it points the other way.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#21

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It · hash: sha256:ae34d909b869c292a1e85700815f920f3cbce0776b2a610f10542a5ac584dd50*

## The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#22

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It · hash: sha256:fcaf391f3630f4f8ed3386d45aa15b18a3ca39ccae166d7b7d2b5821e3238f31*

`OD-SPEC-006` quoted three costs for making the store the durable substrate: stop seeding
from `include_str!` and seed from something committed that is not the record files, with the
bundle named as the candidate; make the files under `docs/records` rendered outputs with a
freshness check; and design a guard, because `OD-SPEC-005` refuses deriving the seeded list
from the directory it is meant to govern.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It · hash: sha256:4a65e8141ba00870af706776590cb3b9eb64ba9fc80fae550b1fcd6da7b406f8*

`OD-SPEC-007` paid the third in general form. It established that what makes that guard a
check is not that its second side is hand-typed into one file, but that the second side is
**authored independently of the directory it is compared against**. Per-record registration
files keep the independence and remove the shared edit. The guard is no longer an open design
question; it is a solved shape with a working instance in this repository.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#24

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It · hash: sha256:72fa23bd0f69cb73ae658b54036c0193aa92034a6d7b61558de174f0474d3add*

The first two costs are the price of **converting governing records**, and this decision does
not convert them. An object family that starts in the store pays neither: there is no seed to
change, because feature requests were never compiled into the binary, and there is no
directory of hand-authored files to turn into rendered outputs, because none was ever
written. Those costs stay owed by whoever later proposes moving governing records, and stay
quoted at `OD-SPEC-007`'s price rather than `OD-SPEC-006`'s.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#25

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / The Price, As OD-SPEC-007 Left It · hash: sha256:4f8ceadc30a76ead35d1d7ba6b239fd32fbe19f4973c4bfdc017c40a605382a0*

What this decision does owe is durability, and that is its real cost, stated plainly: a
born-structured object whose store is rebuilt in memory on every invocation has no substrate
at all.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#26

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds · hash: sha256:a48795084bd5762b8d1615b52e69267fcf9c8e4f8391e9e6825d5aa7c56d06a1*

## What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#27

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds · hash: sha256:082f1a2ee8fb2544cbc05c897fe42decd66f24e5a54abca8f4d833b5526865cf*

One consequence has to be settled now rather than discovered, because getting it wrong is
expensive and the failure is not obvious in a single session.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#28

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds · hash: sha256:dbb56a982e7c5bd899c8c7d64f99bd97a7e17b9d3b69bece93cb067528a1c5ba*

The durable committed form is **text**, not the SQLite file. A binary store in git cannot be
diffed, cannot be reviewed, and cannot be merged — and this repository is worked by
concurrent sessions whose whole coordination model assumes two of them can touch one tree.
Committing the database would make every pair of concurrent feature-request writes a
conflict no tool can resolve.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#29

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds · hash: sha256:d1093741fe8997cb6f5a8348e8de7a46284f45bcd6fd7beb39e5402524d4f750*

So the layering is: the structured record is canonical; its committed durable form is the
deterministic text serialization `nomos-spec-bundle` already produces; SQLite is a derived
working index that any checkout can rebuild; and markdown, YAML, JSON and HTML are
projections of the record, governed by the freshness machinery that already exists.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What Durable Means Here, And What Git Holds · hash: sha256:da76878de3e6ac2fea7586261bf68eff43ef420e267a0b02b0f9a39271a6d639*

`OD-SPEC-006` named the bundle as the candidate for exactly this role. This decision takes it
up for the objects it governs and leaves it a candidate for the ones it does not.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#31

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Binds · hash: sha256:e17d455c073196dc0b82fd16a4f214ba0a125e28874194381ebb7a13f9c38044*

## What This Binds

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#32

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Binds · hash: sha256:ff4b34f305bb0de7a27ea827178b398bd34f3b490d0ca672d0a324d2c4584f66*

It binds the schema of the typed layer. `FeatureRequest`, `DesignSpec` and `FeatureResult`
are defined as structured schemas carrying their own version, validated at write time, with
the obligations `ARC-SPECDB-002` puts on every born-structured object: a versioned schema, a
refusal rather than an acceptance when a submission is incomplete, separation of what was
originally submitted from what was later clarified or inferred, and a freshness proof on
every projection that gets committed.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#33

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Binds · hash: sha256:01905ab4c956a28cecfc30b399629dd76b821a30d84d18d615319501adef812b*

It binds the direction of generation. A `.md`, `.yaml`, `.json` or `.html` document about one
of these objects is an output. Editing one is editing a build artefact, and the surface that
writes them is not an editor.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#34

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:ebcd7ad21b8eb9821a30da3137d2f116568873f3d4d718ec0d464b1a86062e08*

## What This Does Not Bind

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#35

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:2b697f5cc33168fa7a0fb6e422ab5b4912cfef81cb9140f640f5ee82239be415*

It does not touch governing records. They remain document-first, and `OD-SPEC-006` is not
amended.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#36

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:7a28d0aa006b47fb79cdc18eafca746f722d9622f5676fac23a1d06cb41450eb*

It does not touch the imported corpora, the preservation rules, or the round-trip machinery.
Those govern document-first objects and keep governing them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#37

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:74629dd0b6e415a3442957a311af1e20fc3cce935424a591f89bc14ea22ca5cc*

It does not touch `work/ledger.json`. A feature request is not an item, the ledger is not a
specification store, and nothing here makes one answerable to the other.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#38

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:08c8eff51d5267aa80cd8f81e0b65f0cc2f13c16bce8ef3ee0dc97c226fb493d*

It does not decide the physical table layout. That is a separate item, and it inherits a
constraint already written into the schema this repository has: only tables something writes
to exist, because a table nothing writes to looks like a feature in a schema dump and is not
one. Seven tables landing empty ahead of a writer would be that failure committed
deliberately.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#39

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:49e7f0a38ecd6c29ab2ec216625cc17da8bf9c2850e77979b07b1f3f92ed5d63*

It does not decide the intake surface — form, CLI, API or MCP — nor the validation rule set,
including the conditional rules a form contract needs. Those are separate items with their
own predicates. This record decides only where the truth lives.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#40

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Consequences · hash: sha256:89452c3c3f042e75cb1c74f2df2a941f9dbbbad6127f3d11c1fb606337059416*

## Consequences

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#41

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Consequences · hash: sha256:4e9604e525e3cff3633afa93dcddb1889dc87aa6e4c18ce740c6e6387c831087*

The typed layer can be started, which was the thing blocked.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#42

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Consequences · hash: sha256:2299bc37360958514351d7bf6db2958f909ab514c126d602269944bd814d911a*

These objects skip the round-trip proof, because there is no arbitrary document to prove
recoverable. They do not skip proof: they take on a freshness proof instead, and the gate
already runs one such step.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#43

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Feature requests, designs and results are born structured, and their documents are projections / Consequences · hash: sha256:0739bc32bf2eee4ac2f7f0e18545f12a4ef55b594de68a990e442fe69b9cf5db*

Two substrates now exist in one build, deliberately, with a written rule for which side any
object falls on and an argument for why that rule is not a list.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#44

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-008-feature-requests-designs-and-results-are-born-structured-and-their-documents-are-projections.md#45

Accepted. The typed layer is unblocked; durability, physical layout, intake and validation

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#1

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it · hash: sha256:e875d2e85e1968fea8dd452ee18904d3cf8c9909eec17e7319df9fb68d0ea646*

# A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Question · hash: sha256:7ff00c9f54a928d48aa12750281ee8f4ceb18d3a26ba30a189b6cbef37f49d21*

`OD-SPEC-008` made `FeatureRequest`, `DesignSpec` and `FeatureResult` born structured and left
one thing open in the same sentence: the intake surface, listed as form, CLI, API or MCP. That
list is the question as it was first asked, and answering it as asked is the mistake this record
exists to avoid.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Question · hash: sha256:6fb38bfec1c40f69c258d6035293c06724dea77681285dbf8f465015bbbed268*

Nothing writes a submission today. The layout question inherits the constraint that only tables
something writes to exist, so the first writer is also the first table, and whichever surface
gets built first will have decided where validation lives, what a refusal is, and what a
submission is — by existing, in code, rather than in something a reader can disagree with.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Decision · hash: sha256:a15c7c13f167e5ac9204c02acb3f22d9fffdadf996618ee0e068a4b27e4c1511*

## Decision

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Decision · hash: sha256:52e18cef78afd8e85d5c05c91afca65e1c7a1cd706becab1d7a2054f726aa386*

**A submission enters the store through exactly one accept function.** It takes a typed
submission value, decides acceptance or refusal, and is the only path by which a
`FeatureRequest`, `DesignSpec` or `FeatureResult` becomes durable.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Decision · hash: sha256:8a28a13734a8a4c4e24f15fd761b76002355d9f5593a3fe446aa9de2aa7863b2*

**No surface is that door.** A form, a CLI verb, an HTTP endpoint and an MCP tool are
*transports*: each constructs the typed submission from whatever it collects, hands it to the
accept function, and renders the verdict it gets back. A transport that validates, defaults or
persists on its own behalf is a second write door and is a defect, not a variant.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#8

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Decision · hash: sha256:23dd0147b93fa4e7d323c58c90237bf73f5c0704d8dfd38e0828565ffc699699*

**The primary surface is the CLI**, in the sense that it is the first and currently the only
transport this repository will build — `nomos-cli` is the only host that exists, and it is the
only surface the gate can run. It is primary as an adapter and not as an authority. Nothing here
promises a form, an HTTP API or an MCP tool, and none of them is blocked either.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Decision · hash: sha256:a48cdc77787a15d10f32c747ce35ca61381a26612360e951e43fcb492b4e6b6a*

**What surfaces render is the form contract**, not each other. The questions a submission
answers are writable before any submission exists — that is exactly the test `ARC-SPECDB-002`
applies, and it is what made these objects born structured in the first place. So the questions
live in one versioned contract, and a transport is a rendering of it: a CLI verb, a set of form
fields, a tool schema. Two transports disagreeing about which questions exist is then a defect
in one rendering rather than a difference of opinion between products.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong · hash: sha256:02928476bab8823ee13951279ffa11eebe8d60731abfaf5fcc9a5ba66cefa54b*

## Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong · hash: sha256:27ebf4d811c8e704843a92796522ed4c21e1348050cf44621200d2a327e3fd59*

Picking one of *form, CLI, API, MCP* as the canonical surface answers a question about
transport with a decision about authority, and the two failures it produces are already
recorded elsewhere in this repository.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong · hash: sha256:135959a7014186867a6e7150b0bee37b12fb8b39087020b234b25777a110cdf7*

**It puts the rule set in a transport.** `ARC-SPECDB-002` charges every born-structured object
with validation at write time that refuses an incomplete submission. If the CLI is the door,
that refusal is CLI code. The second transport then either re-derives the rules or calls into
the first one, and re-derived rules drift with nothing able to notice. `P10-SERVICE-SEAM` names
precisely this shape for the work verbs — a second adapter having to re-derive the claim, lease
and finish sequence rather than call it — and observes that it is cheapest to settle while there
is one adapter. Intake has zero adapters, which is cheaper still.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#13

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong · hash: sha256:ba39561cdb7c9a2361ae21d6171330c1f265427e9ad373f516db3c0e726196b2*

**It contradicts the shape the store band already uses.** `nomos-store` is described in one line
as content-addressed documents *with one write door per authority*. Intake is a write door onto
an authority. Giving it one door is applying an existing shape, and giving it one door per
surface would be the first place in this workspace where the number of write doors is decided by
the number of user interfaces.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#14

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Why Answering The List Would Be Wrong · hash: sha256:a5b22ad9c5640180de6c8efe4bc8377c21fbaaab8d60484588c2a79e1d4ca649*

**It fixes a list.** The four named surfaces are the ones somebody could think of while writing
`OD-SPEC-008`. A rule that names them answers for those four and produces nothing for the fifth,
which is the failure `ARC-SPECDB-002` refused when it declined an artifact-kind axis. A rule
about the relationship between a transport and the door answers for surfaces nobody has proposed.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#15

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What Crosses The Seam · hash: sha256:2f8a5c7873df7b18d8dd09ae8acf12b2b90b1f058c0d5e73ad2f36950884ea4f*

## What Crosses The Seam

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#16

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What Crosses The Seam · hash: sha256:999b5e340678280616467c3dd93624e3554c074f4cc83b5c2394a11a5b8dc6b5*

A **submission** is what a transport hands to the accept function. Three properties are fixed
here because they are properties of the seam rather than of the rule set:

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#17

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What Crosses The Seam · hash: sha256:078263bcb9f5306d336b50742a8c37b0afce921ddff15e7252aaf25fb30e8920*

- It carries what was submitted **verbatim**, separately from anything the transport supplied.
  A default a CLI filled in, a field a form pre-populated and a value an agent inferred are not
  submitted content, and `ARC-SPECDB-002` requires the two never be merged into one field that
  no longer says which it is. A transport that folds its defaults into the submitted text
  destroys that distinction before the door can see it, so the door cannot be the place it is
  first enforced.
- It names the form contract version it was constructed against, so a submission written under
  an older set of questions is readable as that shape rather than silently reinterpreted.
- It is **complete or refused, never partially stored**. A draft that has not passed validation
  is not a stored submission with missing fields; what a draft is, and where it lives, is
  `OD-SPEC-010`.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#18

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What This Binds · hash: sha256:e17d455c073196dc0b82fd16a4f214ba0a125e28874194381ebb7a13f9c38044*

## What This Binds

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#19

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What This Binds · hash: sha256:3bf0d4e5515406de3712ecc6a311edbc0a57564adda89803b2dffd0e316b1d60*

Every transport, present and future, constructs a submission and calls the accept function.
There is no second path to durability for these three objects.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#20

The form contract is a versioned artifact that transports render. Its content — which questions
are required, which are conditional and on what — is `OD-SPEC-010` and is not decided here.

The CLI transport is the one that gets built, and it is built as a transport: a verb that
collects, calls and renders. If it grows validation of its own, that is a regression against

## What This Does Not Bind

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#23

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / What This Does Not Bind · hash: sha256:13f77480415f75376b786b4cea43cbece81b22a04cabbd26d307cc0b186db3eb*

**It does not decide where the accept function lives.** Which crate holds application
orchestration, and whether choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome are
separated at all, is `P10-SERVICE-SEAM`'s subject and belongs to the record that item writes.
This record says there is one door and that surfaces are transports onto it; it deliberately
says nothing about the module it sits in, because that answer must serve the work verbs too and
this is not the item that can see them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#24

It does not decide the validation rule set, the refusal vocabulary, or the draft state. That is
`OD-SPEC-010`.

It does not decide the physical layout, the table set, or what the accept function writes. That
is `OD-SPEC-013`, which lands the layout together with the first writer because a table nothing
writes to may not exist.

It does not touch `work/ledger.json`. A submission is not an item, and `OD-SPEC-008` already

## Controls

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-009-a-submission-enters-through-one-accept-function-and-every-surface-is-a-transport-onto-it.md#30

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: A submission enters through one accept function, and every surface is a transport onto it / Controls · hash: sha256:b570e25198c8af9236c50eff72f5cb15dd5c26c67e3ff765c2ad3424f0bb9701*

| Weakening | What it produces |
|---|---|
| the CLI verb validates before calling | the rule set lives in a transport, and the second transport re-derives it |
| each surface persists what it collects | one write door per interface; a submission means something different depending on where it entered |
| the transport merges its defaults into submitted text | `ARC-SPECDB-002`'s submitted-versus-inferred separation is destroyed upstream of every reader |
| the submission carries no contract version | a request written under older questions is reinterpreted rather than read as what it was |
| a draft is stored as an incomplete submission | validation stops being a refusal and becomes a later reader's problem, which is what born-structured was supposed to buy out of |
| the door is named as the CLI | the fifth surface reopens this decision, and the list decides it again |

`P10-SERVICE-SEAM` gains a second case rather than a competitor. It asks where orchestration

# Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#2

*revision: authored · kind: heading · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:68b4fb6c30734f663071fbcaf8da5c1d5e4422686bff1353d95e9dca1b326e23*

## Question

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#3

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:2fb551117bf89ea3230de1a3ae822088337221d848bbb3a75be5d97a9ec45807*

`ARC-SPECDB-002` charges every born-structured object with validation at write time that
refuses an incomplete submission rather than accepting it, and with keeping what was
originally submitted apart from what was later clarified, inferred or decided. `OD-SPEC-008`
applies that charge to feature requests, designs and results, and defers the rule set —
including the conditional rules a form contract needs.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#4

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:18377905a179291269b1f252b7f62535fbeadbcf921753bae268a76620135b30*

Until the rules are written down the first writer encodes them, and a rule encoded in a
writer cannot be read, cited or disagreed with. This record states them.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#5

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:b00bfe8b707f62428fa68e88abbc8cc165fd86a5b2333dd189a080a2e3b71d4e*

It decides no physical layout, which is `OD-SPEC-013`'s. The intake surface is already
decided: `OD-SPEC-009` landed while this record was being written, and put every submission
through one accept function, with transports forbidden from validating. That makes this record
the content of the check that function performs, and the two fit without either being bent —
`OD-SPEC-009` fixed where validation happens and explicitly deferred what it checks, the
refusal vocabulary and the draft state to here.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#6

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:d5b273a63acfa998dd660491b5b656977b8a75b995933392070c7d3d53a66112*

(This citation, and the two below, named `OD-SPEC-011` in version 1. That identifier was
reserved for the layout decision by `P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT`, and was then published for an
unrelated decision — an unknown relation type refused by name — by a second item that had
reserved it independently; nothing checked that two items had reserved one identifier.
`OD-SPEC-013` is the record the layout decision actually landed under. `OD-SPEC-013`'s own
*Why This Record Is Not `OD-SPEC-011`* section carries the fuller account.)

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#7

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / Question · hash: sha256:0bf5b5a4877a3955311ad89ae46e0cd4885952ae5f8a6d6413333b4fe404a824*

The rules below are properties of a submission, not of a door. They are the same rules
whichever transport constructs it and whichever table it lands in. A rule set that had to be
re-argued per surface would be a rule set that lives in the surface, which is the failure
`OD-SPEC-009` refused.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#8

## The Test For Requiredness

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#9

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / The Test For Requiredness · hash: sha256:9f1c938d485288140795279028f6d078951815e40421c4992c19c7d0502ef000*

A list of required fields answers for the fields on the list and produces nothing for the
next field, which is the failure `ARC-SPECDB-002` refuses on the substrate axis. The same
refusal applies here, so requiredness is decided by a test rather than enumerated by
preference:

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#10

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / The Test For Requiredness · hash: sha256:d2bd4a81fab377da18a1fc367c1398feb7b3cd17b5de858272b1adba88f9980e*

> A field is **required** when its absence cannot be repaired by a later reader without
> asking the submitter again.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#11

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / The Test For Requiredness · hash: sha256:5eb69f288252a68d8d7f0add4072336d9279aff4aba22b8b7747e171018f6985*

That is the whole criterion, and it has a direction. `goal` is required because nobody can
recover why a thing was wanted from the thing itself. An estimate is not required because a
later reader can produce one, and a wrong estimate is visible as an estimate. The test is
answerable about a field nobody has proposed yet, which is the property it exists to have.

### docs/records/OD-SPEC-010-validation-refuses-what-cannot-be-repaired-later-and-no-later-value-overwrites-what-was-submitted.md#12

*revision: authored · kind: prose · heading: Validation refuses what cannot be repaired later, and no later value overwrites what was submitted / The Test For Requiredness · hash: sha256:4d3e91aabf29948cf34ed7dbb04ccb2c7dc8df7b03be9d46ed614f02ca47933f*

The field sets below are that test applied, not an independent authority. A field added later
argues from the test; a field dropped later argues against it.
